A <DROP-OUT FUSE> is a <FUSE> in which the fuse-carrier automatically drops into a position providing an isolating distance after the fuse has operated.
<DROPPING> is the <Activity> of falling or letting fall in any way

A <DROPPING POINT> is an <IndirectProperty> assigned to a grease composition representing the corrected temperature at which the first drop of material falls from the test cup and reaches the bottom of the test tube. Ref ISO 1998 def. 2-021
A <DRUM> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <CONTAINER> with a <CYLINDER(shape)> shape, used for shipping bulk cargo

<DRUM FILLING> is the <Activity> of to fill drums
A <DRUM RECORDER> is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and a <RECORDER> in which the chart is wrapped as a single turn around a cylindrical drum which is rotated by the chart driving mechanism

<DRY> is a <INDIVIDUAL WITH A STATUS> that is free from moisture or liquid

description: A <DRY AND VENTILATED ENVIRONMENT> is an <ENVIRONMENT> that is dry and ventilated

description: A <DRY CHEMICAL FIXED UNIT> is a <DRY CHEMICAL EXTINGUISHER> that is fixed at a location

It is calculated as alpha_ij = delta p_i/delta E_j where p_i is the cartesian component along the i-axis of the electric dipole moment induced by the applied  <ELECTRIC FIELD STRENGTH> acting on the molecule, and E_j is the component along the j_axis of this  <ELECTRIC FIELD STRENGTH>

<GALVANISING> is the <Activity> of coating (layer covering) with zinc, typically for iron and steel

<GALVANIZING> is the <Activity> of applying a protective zinc coating to steel or iron, to prevent rusting. The most common method is hot-dip galvanizing, in which the parts are submerged in a bath of molten <ZINC>

<GANGING> is the <Activity> of assembling or operating (mechanical or electronic parts) simultaneously as a group

A <GAS DETECTING INSTRUMENT - ULTRASONIC> is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and a <GAS DETECTING INSTRUMENT> that handles the measurement result from a <GAS DETECTING MEASURING ELEMENT - ULTRASONIC>

description: A <GAS DETECTING MEASURING ELEMENT - ELECTROCHEMICAL> is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and a <GAS DETECTING MEASURING ELEMENT> where gases are allowed to diffuse through a porous membrane to an electrode where it is either chemically oxidized or reduced. The amount of current produced is determined by how much of the gas is oxidized at the electrode, indicating the concentration of the gas
superclasses: GAS DETECTING MEASURING ELEMENT, INSTRUMENTATION ITEM

description: A <GAS DETECTING MEASURING ELEMENT - HOLOGRAPHIC> is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and a <GAS DETECTING MEASURING ELEMENT>using light reflection to detect changes in a polymer film matrix containing a hologram. Since holograms reflect light at certain wavelengths, a change in their composition can generate a colorful reflection indicating the presence of a gas molecule
superclasses: GAS DETECTING MEASURING ELEMENT, INSTRUMENTATION ITEM

uniqueName: GAS DETECTING MEASURING ELEMENT - INFRARED IMAGING
description: A <GAS DETECTING MEASURING ELEMENT - INFRARED IMAGING> is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and a <GAS DETECTING MEASURING ELEMENT> that can be an active or passive system. For active sensing, IR imaging sensors typically scan a laser across the field of view of a scene and look for backscattered light at the absorption line wavelength of a specific target gas. Passive IR imaging sensors measure spectral changes at each pixel in an image and look for specific spectral signatures that indicate the presence of target gases
superclasses: GAS DETECTING MEASURING ELEMENT, INSTRUMENTATION ITEM

uniqueName: GAS DETECTING MEASURING ELEMENT - INFRARED POINT
description: A <GAS DETECTING MEASURING ELEMENT - INFRARED POINT> is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and a <GAS DETECTING MEASURING ELEMENT> using radiation passing through a known volume of gas; energy from the sensor beam is absorbed at certain wavelengths, depending on the properties of the specific gas
superclasses: GAS DETECTING MEASURING ELEMENT, INSTRUMENTATION ITEM

description: A <GAS DETECTING MEASURING ELEMENT - SEMICONDUCTOR> is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and a <GAS DETECTING MEASURING ELEMENT> using a chemical reaction that takes place, causing the electrical resistance in the sensor to be decreased when it comes in contact with the monitored gas
superclasses: GAS DETECTING MEASURING ELEMENT, INSTRUMENTATION ITEM

description: A <GAS DETECTING MEASURING ELEMENT - ULTRASONIC> is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and  a <GAS DETECTING MEASURING ELEMENT> using acoustic sensors to detect changes in the background noise of its environment
superclasses: GAS DETECTING MEASURING ELEMENT, INSTRUMENTATION ITEM

A <GAS REVERSAL CHAMBER> is a <CHAMBER> that is part of a boiler and is used to reverse the flow of combustion gasses

A <GAS SWEETENING SYSTEM> is a <SYSTEM> for removal of sour substances as H2S and CO2

subclasses: CHARGE AIR SUPPLY SYSTEM, GAS COMPRESSION SYSTEM, INERT GAS SYSTEM, SCAVENGING/CHARGE AIR SYSTEM, UTILITY GAS SYSTEM

subclasses: AIR, CO2 GAS, EXHAUST GAS, EXTINGUISHING GAS, FIRE EXTINGUISHER PROPELLANT GAS, FLUE GAS, FUEL GAS, HELIUM GAS, HYDROCARBON GAS, HYDROGEN SULFIDE, METHANE GAS, NATURAL GAS, NITROGEN GAS, NITROGEN OXIDE, SULFUR HEXAFLUORIDE, TRACER GAS, WATER GAS

uniqueName: GAS-OIL RATIO DURING TEST AT STANDARD CONDITIONS
description: A <GAS-OIL RATIO DURING TEST AT STANDARD CONDITIONS> is a <GAS-OIL RATIO AT T AND P> that is the ratio between the volume of gas compared to the volume of oil during a test. Both volumes should be converted to the same pressure and temperature (generally to standard conditions, i.e. 15 deg. C and 1 atm)

uniqueName: GAS-OIL RATIO DURING TEST AT UPPER LIMIT FLOW CONDITIONS

superclasses: GAS-OIL RATIO AT T AND P

uniqueName: GAS-OIL RATIO FOR EXPORT AT STANDARD CONDITIONS
description: A <GAS-OIL RATIO FOR EXPORT AT STANDARD CONDITIONS> is a <GAS OIL RATIO AT STANDARD CONDITIONS> at standard conditions that is the ratio of the exported gas volume and the oil volume. Both volume flow rates should be converted to the same pressure and temperature (generally to standard conditions, i.e. 15 deg. C and 1 atm)

subclasses: BELLOW SEALED GATE VALVE, CLAMP GATE VALVE, COMPACT GATE VALVE, CONDUIT GATE VALVE, GATE CONTROL VALVE, HOSE GATE VALVE, KNIFE GATE VALVE, PARALLEL GATE VALVE, PENSTOCK VALVE, ROTARY GATE VALVE, SLIDE GATE VALVE, SPLIT GATE VALVE, WEDGE GATE VALVE

subclasses: KNIFE GATE, PARALLEL GATE, SLAB GATE, SPLIT GATE, WEDGE GATE

description: A <GATE VALVE STEM SEAL> is a <VALVE STEM SEAL> that is intended for a gate valve.
A <GATE VALVE YOKE> is a <VALVE YOKE> by which the valve operator (actuator or hand wheel) is supported rigidly to the bonnet assembly of a gate valve.

<GATE-TO-GATE> is the <Activity> of process where all production stages occur within one site. The site may be geographically specified, or in the case of e.g. average data, the geographical specification may be more general. Processes outside the defined gates are <NOT> included
<GATE-TO-GRAVE> is the <Activity> of process that includes the distribution, the use and the final disposal of the product
<GATHERING> is the <Activity> of bringing together and taking in from scattered places or sources
A <GAUGE> is a <FunctionalObject> that is capable of <MEASURING> and <INDICATING> without auxiliary energy supply
subclasses: PROCESS GAUGE, TANK GAUGE

description: A <GAUGE PRESSURE> is a <PRESSURE> that is relative to the local atmosperic pressure
A <GAUGE PRESSURE GAUGE> is a <PRESSURE GAUGE> and a <GAUGE PRESSURE MEASURING INSTRUMENT>
superclasses: GAUGE PRESSURE MEASURING INSTRUMENT, PRESSURE GAUGE
subclasses: PRESSURE MEMORY GAUGE

description: A <GAUGE PRESSURE MEASURING ELEMENT> is a <PRESSURE MEASURING ELEMENT> for the measurement of <GAUGE PRESSURE>
subclasses: DIAPHRAGM SEAL ASSEMBLY, GAUGE PRESSURE MEASURING ELEMENT - BELLOWS, GAUGE PRESSURE MEASURING ELEMENT - BOURDON, GAUGE PRESSURE MEASURING ELEMENT - CAPSULE, GAUGE PRESSURE MEASURING ELEMENT - DIAPHRAGM, GAUGE PRESSURE MEASURING ELEMENT - DIAPHRAGM SEAL, GAUGE PRESSURE MEASURING ELEMENT - LIQUID COLUMN, GAUGE PRESSURE MEASURING ELEMENT - TOTAL PRESSURE CELL

superclasses: GAUGE PRESSURE MEASURING ELEMENT, INSTRUMENTATION ITEM

description: A <GAUGE PRESSURE MEASURING ELEMENT - BOURDON> is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and  a <GAUGE PRESSURE MEASURING ELEMENT> that is a radially-formed tube with an oval crosssection. The pressure of the media acts on the inside of this tube. The end of the tube which is not fixed moves, and this movement is a measurement for the pressure
superclasses: GAUGE PRESSURE MEASURING ELEMENT, INSTRUMENTATION ITEM

description: A <GAUGE PRESSURE MEASURING ELEMENT - CAPSULE>  is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and  a <GAUGE PRESSURE MEASURING ELEMENT> that is an element that comprises two circular-shaped, corrugated diaphragms, joined together around the rim with a pressure-tight seal. The pressure acts on the inside of this capsule and the generated stroke movement is indicated by means of a movement as a measurement of pressure
superclasses: GAUGE PRESSURE MEASURING ELEMENT, INSTRUMENTATION ITEM

description: A <GAUGE PRESSURE MEASURING ELEMENT - DIAPHRAGM> is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and a <GAUGE PRESSURE MEASURING ELEMENT> that is a circular-shaped, corrugated membrane, either clamped around the rim between two flanges or welded and subject to the pressure of the media acting on one side. The deflection caused in this way is used as a measurement for pressure.
superclasses: GAUGE PRESSURE MEASURING ELEMENT, INSTRUMENTATION ITEM
subclasses: GAUGE PRESSURE TRANSDUCER

uniqueName: GAUGE PRESSURE MEASURING ELEMENT - DIAPHRAGM SEAL
description: A <GAUGE PRESSURE MEASURING ELEMENT - DIAPHRAGM SEAL> is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and a <GAUGE PRESSURE MEASURING ELEMENT> where the <CONNECTION POINT> is equipped with a <DIAPHRAGM SEAL>
superclasses: GAUGE PRESSURE MEASURING ELEMENT, INSTRUMENTATION ITEM

uniqueName: GAUGE PRESSURE MEASURING ELEMENT - LIQUID COLUMN
description: A <GAUGE PRESSURE MEASURING ELEMENT - LIQUID COLUMN> is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and a <GAUGE PRESSURE MEASURING ELEMENT> for low pressures, where the pressure is counterbalanced by a liquid column
superclasses: GAUGE PRESSURE MEASURING ELEMENT, INSTRUMENTATION ITEM

uniqueName: GAUGE PRESSURE MEASURING ELEMENT - TOTAL PRESSURE CELL
description: A <GAUGE PRESSURE MEASURING ELEMENT - TOTAL PRESSURE CELL>  is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and  a <GAUGE PRESSURE MEASURING ELEMENT> that is formed from two circular plates of stainless steel. The edges of the plates are welded together to form a sealed cavity, which is filled with fluid. Then a pressure transducer is attached to the cell. The cell is installed with its sensitive surface in direct contact with the soil. The total pressure acting on that surface is transmitted to the fluid inside the cell and measured by the pressure transducer
superclasses: GAUGE PRESSURE MEASURING ELEMENT, INSTRUMENTATION ITEM

description: A <GAUGE PRESSURE MEASURING INSTRUMENT> is a <PRESSURE MEASURING INSTRUMENT> for the measurement of <GAUGE PRESSURE>, that handles the measurement result from a <GAUGE PRESSURE MEASURING ELEMENT>
subclasses: GAUGE PRESSURE GAUGE, GAUGE PRESSURE MEASURING INSTRUMENT - BELLOWS, GAUGE PRESSURE MEASURING INSTRUMENT - DIAPHRAGM SEAL, GAUGE PRESSURE MEASURING INSTRUMENT -BOURDON, GAUGE PRESSURE SWITCH, GAUGE PRESSURE TRANSMITTER

A <HEXAGONAL CLOSE PACKED (HCP) STRUCTURE> is an <ArrangedIndividual> that has a crystalline structure of alternating layers, shifted so its atoms are aligned to the gaps of the preceding layer. The atoms from one layer nest themselves in the empty space between the atoms of the adjacent layer just like in the fcc structure. However, instead of being a cubic structure, the pattern is hexagonal. The hcp structure has three layers of atoms. In each the top and bottom layer, there are six atoms that arrange themselves in the shape of a hexagon and a seventh atom that sits in the middle of the hexagon. The middle layer has three atoms nestle in the triangular "grooves" of the top and bottom plane. Note that there are six of these "grooves" surrounding each atom in the hexagonal plane, but only three of them can be filled by atoms. There are six atoms in the hcp unit cell. Each of the 12 atoms in the corners of the top and bottom layers contribute 1/6 atom to the unit cell, the two atoms in the center of the hexagon of both the top and bottom layers each contribute 1/2 atom and each of the three atom in the middle layer contribute 1 atom. The image on the right above attempts to show several hcp unit cells in a larger lattice. The coordination number of the atoms in this structure is 12. There are six nearest neighbors in the same close packed layer, three in the layer above and three in the layer below. The packing factor is 0.74, which is the same as the fcc unit cell

HIGH TEMPERATURE HYDROGEN ATTACK is a <DESTRUCTIVE ACTION> which concerns steels operating at elevated temperatures (typically above 400&amp;#176;C) in hydrogen environments. It iresults in hydrogen dissociating and dissolving in the steel, and then reacting with the carbon in solution in the steel to form methane. This can result in either surface decarburisation, when the reaction mostly occurs at the surface and draws carbon from the material, or internal decarburisation when atomic hydrogen penetrates the material and reacts with carbon to form methane, which accumulates at grain boundaries and/or precipitate interfaces, and cannot diffuse out of the steel. This causes the fissures and cracking which are typical of HTHA
<HIGH TEMPERATURE OXIDATION> is <CORROSION> that refers to a chemical reaction involving a metallic object and atmospheric oxygen that produces corrosion at elevated temperatures

description: A <HYDRAULIC GOVERNOR> is a <SPEED GOVERNOR> that is provided with a special centrifugal pump as speed-sensing element
A <HYDRAULIC HATCHWAY COVER> is a <HATCHWAY COVER> that is hydraulically operated.
A <HYDRAULIC HOSE> is a <HOSE> that is designed and approved for being used as a hydraulic hose.
A <HYDRAULIC IMPULSE TURBINE> is a <IMPULSE TURBINE> in which a liquid acts chiefly by its kinetic energy
subclasses: PELTON TURBINE

description: A <HYDRAULIC JACK> is a <LIFTING JACK> in which the lifting head is carried on a plunger working in a cylinder, to which oil or water is supplied under pressure from a pump
A <HYDRAULIC LINER HANGER> is a <LINER HANGER> which set liners in casing by pressurizing the work string to set the slips. Work string manipulation need not be considered for setting operations.
A <HYDRAULIC LOAD CELL> is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and  a <WEIGHT MEASURING ELEMENT> that is a conventional piston and cylinder arrangement
A <HYDRAULIC MOTOR> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <MOTOR> and a <HYDRAULIC TO ROTATION ENERGY CONVERTER> that is intended to generate power by means of high pressure oil
superclasses: ARTEFACT, HYDRAULIC TO ROTATION ENERGY CONVERTER, MOTOR
subclasses: HYDRAULIC RECIPROCATING MOTOR, HYDRAULIC ROTARY MOTOR, HYDRAULIC STARTING MOTOR

description: A <HYDRAULIC NOZZLE> is a <NOZZLE> intended for connecting hydraulic units
A <HYDRAULIC PISTON ACTUATOR> is a <HYDRAULIC ACTUATOR> that is intended to operate by a displacement of a piston using hydraulic energy
subclasses: DOUBLE ACTING HYDRAULIC PISTON ACTUATOR, HYDRAULIC PISTON ACTUATOR SPRING RETURN, SINGLE ACTING HYDRAULIC PISTON ACTUATOR

description: A <HYDRAULIC PISTON ACTUATOR SPRING RETURN> is a <HYDRAULIC PISTON ACTUATOR> and a <SPRING RETURN ACTUATOR> with a spring acting on one side of the piston
superclasses: HYDRAULIC PISTON ACTUATOR, SPRING RETURN ACTUATOR

description: A <HYDRAULIC POWER> is a <POWER> transmitted by the controlled circulation of pressurized fluid, usually a water-soluble oil or waterâ€“glycol mixture, to a motor that converts it into a mechanical output capable of doing work on a load

A <HYDRAULIC POWER RECOVERY TURBINE>, also referred to as HPRT, is a <HYDRAULIC TURBINE> that is used in a process when a fluid is pressurized and must be reduced in pressure. Rather than throttle the fluid pressure though a pressure reducing valve (PRV) and waste the stored energy, a PRT can be used to drop the fluid pressure and turn the turbine impeller and drive a generator or drive shaft to another process.
A <HYDRAULIC POWER SUPPLY> is an <ENERGY SUPPLY> that supplies hydraulic power
subclasses: HYDRAULIC POWER UNIT

description: A <HYDRAULIC POWER UNIT> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <HYDRAULIC POWER SUPPLY> and that is a unit that is, as a minimum, consisting of a engine driven hydraulic pump and a reservoir which is delivering hydraulic energy to one or more consumers
A <HYDRAULIC PRESS> is a <PRESS(machine)> and a <HYDRAULIC APPARATUS> that is hydraulically powered and is upstroke, downstroke or horizontal

A <HYDRAULIC PUMP> is a <POSITIVE DISPLACEMENT PUMP> used in hydraulic drive systems and can be hydrostatic or hydrodynamic. It is a mechanical source of power that converts mechanical power into hydraulic energy (hydrostatic energy i.e. flow, pressure). It generates flow with enough power to overcome pressure induced by the load at the pump outlet. When a hydraulic pump operates, creates a vacuum at the pump inlet, which forces liquid from the reservoir into the inlet line to the pump and by mechanical action delivers this liquid to the pump outlet and forces it into the hydraulic system.
A <HYDRAULIC REACTION TURBINE> is a <REACTION TURBINE> that converts the potential energy of a flowing liquid to rotational energy for further use
subclasses: AXIAL HYDRAULIC REACTION TURBINE, FRANCIS TURBINE, HYDRAULIC POWER RECOVERY TURBINE, WATER TURBINE

description: A <HYDRAULIC RECIPROCATING MOTOR> is a <HYDRAULIC MOTOR> that uses a reciprocating motion which usually is converted into rotary motion
A <HYDRAULIC ROTARY MOTOR> is a <HYDRAULIC MOTOR> that uses a vane-rotor or a gear-rotor to convert pressure energy into rotational energy
A <HYDRAULIC SHOCK ABSORBER> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <SHOCK ABSORBER> that uses a cylinder filled with a hydraulic fluid
A <HYDRAULIC SIGNAL> is an <InformationObject> and a <SIGNAL> that is based on variations in <PRESSURE> in a <LIQUID COMPOUND>, usually a <HYDRAULIC FLUID>
A <HYDRAULIC SIGNAL CONVEYOR> is a <SIGNAL CONVEYOR>s
A <HYDRAULIC START SYSTEM> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <START SYSTEM> that uses pressurized liquid as a power source to start a driver
A <HYDRAULIC STARTER> is a <HYDRAULIC APPARATUS> and a <STARTER> in which the force for closing the main contacts is provided exclusively by hydraulic energy
A <HYDRAULIC STARTING MOTOR> is a <HYDRAULIC MOTOR> and a <STARTING MOTOR>
A <HYDRAULIC STEPPING ACTUATOR> is a <STEPPING ACTUATOR> having a hydraulic motor
A <HYDRAULIC SWITCH> is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and a <SWITCHING DEVICE> intended to switch one or more hydraulic signals
subclasses: INSTRUMENT MANIFOLD

description: A <HYDRAULIC SWIVEL JOINT> is an <ARTEFACT> and a  <SWIVEL JOINT> that is used in a hydraulic system
A <HYDRAULIC TO MECHANICAL ENERGY CONVERTER> is an <ENERGY CONVERTER> that is capable of <HYDRAULIC TO MECHANICAL ENERGY CONVERTING>
subclasses: HYDRAULIC TO ROTATION ENERGY CONVERTER, HYDRAULICALLY ACTUATED ARTEFACT

description: <HYDRAULIC TO MECHANICAL ENERGY CONVERTING> is <ENERGY CONVERTING> to convert hydraulic energy into mechanical energy
A <HYDRAULIC TO ROTATION ENERGY CONVERTER> is an <HYDRAULIC TO MECHANICAL ENERGY CONVERTER> that is capable of <HYDRAULIC TO ROTATION ENERGY CONVERTING>
subclasses: HYDRAULIC MOTOR

description: <HYDRAULIC TO ROTATION ENERGY CONVERTING> is <POTENTIAL TO MECHANICAL ENERGY CONVERTING> of hydraulic energy in a <LIQUID> into mechanical energy by expansion in a rotational device (i.e. in a hydraulic turbine)
A <HYDRAULIC TOP DRIVE DRILLING SYSTEM> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <TOP DRIVE DRILLING SYSTEM> and a <HYDRAULICALLY ACTUATED ARTEFACT> that is powered using hydraulic motors
superclasses: ARTEFACT, HYDRAULICALLY ACTUATED ARTEFACT, TOP DRIVE DRILLING SYSTEM

description: A <HYDRAULIC TORQUE CONVERTER> is <FLUID COUPLING> allowing a smooth start of a driven equiment and then keeping a nearly constant speed
subclasses: HYDRODYNAMIC DRIVE, HYDROKINETIC DRIVE, HYDROVISCOUS DRIVE

description: A <HYDRAULIC TORSIONAL VIBRATION DAMPER> is a <TORSIONAL VIBRATION DAMPER> where the turning mass is connected to the driver plate by means of hydraulic loaded friction linings
<HYDRAULIC TRANSPORT> is <TRANSPORTING> by means of hydraulic means, such as a carrier gas or fluid
A <HYDRAULIC VALVE ACTUATOR> is a <HYDRAULIC ACTUATOR> and a <CONTROLLED VALVE ACTUATOR> that is designed to operate a valve
A <HYDRAULIC VALVE LIFT SYSTEM> is a <FLUID SYSTEM> using hydraulic fluid (oil) to operate the cylinder valves
A <HYDRAULIC VARIABLE SPEED GEARBOX> is a <VARIABLE SPEED GEARBOX> that is hydraulically operated.
A <HYDRAULICALLY ACTUATED ARTEFACT> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <HYDRAULIC TO MECHANICAL ENERGY CONVERTER> that is actuated by hydraulic power
superclasses: ARTEFACT, HYDRAULIC TO MECHANICAL ENERGY CONVERTER
subclasses: HYDRAULIC ACTUATOR, HYDRAULIC TOP DRIVE DRILLING SYSTEM, HYDRAULICALLY ACTUATED DIAPHRAGM PUMP, HYDRAULICALLY ACTUATED SWITCH, HYDRAULICALLY ACTUATED VALVE

description: A <HYDRAULICALLY ACTUATED DIAPHRAGM PUMP> is a <CONTROLLED VOLUME DIAPHRAGM PUMP> and a <HYDRAULICALLY ACTUATED ARTEFACT> where the diaphragm is hydraulically coupled to a piston or plunger. The piston or plunger is moving hydraulic liquid in and out of a chamber behind the diaphragm. The diaphragm separates hydraulic and pumped liquid
superclasses: CONTROLLED VOLUME DIAPHRAGM PUMP, HYDRAULICALLY ACTUATED ARTEFACT

description: A <HYDRAULICALLY ACTUATED SWITCH> is a <MECHANICALLY ACTUATED SWITCH> and a <HYDRAULICALLY ACTUATED ARTEFACT> that is actuated by a <HYDRAULIC ACTUATOR>
superclasses: HYDRAULICALLY ACTUATED ARTEFACT, MECHANICALLY ACTUATED SWITCH

description: A <HYDRAULICALLY ACTUATED VALVE> is an <ACTUATED VALVE> and a <HYDRAULICALLY ACTUATED ARTEFACT> operated by an hydraulic actuator
<HYDRO POWER GENERATING> is <POWER GENERATING> by means of a <HYDROELECTRIC POWER GENERATOR>
<HYDROCARBON> is an <ORGANIC MOLECULE> consisting only of carbon and hydrogen. There are three main classes; saturated, unsaturated, and aromatic hydrocarbons
subclasses: AROMATIC HYDROCARBON, SATURATED HYDROCARBON, UNSATURATED HYDROCARBON

description: <HYDROCARBON ACCOUNTING> is <ACCOUNTING> of all of the hydrocarbon fluids into and out of Stock (i.e., Inventory) which includes all storage facilities at a site including fluid within a pipeline
<HYDROCARBON ASH> is <ASH> that consists of incombustible components of a burnt hydrocarbon mixture
A <HYDROCARBON CARBON RESIDUE> is a <MINERAL OIL> that is a carbon residue in a hydrocarbon mixture

A <HYDROCARBON CATALYTIC FINES> is a <MINERAL OIL> that consists of particles of the catalyst (often aluminium and silica oxides) used in the refinery process which have been carried over into the refined hydrocarbon fractions

A <HYDROCARBON COMPOUND> is an <ORGANIC COMPOUND> comprising hydrogen and carbon. Hydrocarbons can be as simple as methane [CH4], but many are highly complex molecules, and can occur as gases, liquids or solids. The molecules can have the shape of chains, branching chains, rings or other structures
subclasses: BENZENE TOLUENE ETHYLBENZENE AND XYLENE COMPOUND

description: A <HYDROCARBON GAS> is a <GASEOUS COMPOUND> found in the earth formed of carbon and hydrogen atoms. Hydrocarbon gas can be composed of methane, ethane, butane, propane, nitrogen, carbon dioxide, hexane, heptanes, and pentane
A <HYDROCARBON LEAK DETECTOR> is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and a <FLUID LEAK DETECTOR> designed to detect hydrocarbons
A <HYDROCARBON SEDIMENT> is a <MINERAL OIL> that is a hydrocarbon blend consisting of hydrocarbon sludges and extraneous materials
A <HYDROCARBON SHOWS RESULT> is a <REPORT> about a test result that indicates whether hydrocarbons are observed or not in a hydrocarbon shows testing

<HYDROCARBON SHOWS TESTING> is <TESTING> that consist in a surface observation of hydrocarbons, usually observed as fluorescent liquid on cuttings when viewed with an ultraviolet or black light (oil show) or increased gas readings from the mud logger's gas-detection equipment (gas show)
An <HYDROCARBONS IN WATER DETECTOR> is a <DETECTOR> using an <ANALYSIS MEASURING ELEMENT> for detection of hydrocarbons in water

<HYDROCHLORIC ACID CORROSION> is an <ACIDIC CORROSION> due to the existence of a large amount of highly active chloride ions, it can destroy the passivation film on the surface of the metal material, causing comprehensive corrosion of the material, pitting corrosion and stress corrosion cracking of stainless steel
<HYDROCHLORINATING> is the <Activity> of treating or combining with hydrochloric acid or hydrogen chloride
A <HYDROCRACKER> is a <CRACKER> that has the capability of <HYDROCRACKING>
subclasses: HYDROCRACKER REACTOR

description: A <HYDROCRACKER REACTOR> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <HYDROCRACKER> and a <CHEMICAL REACTOR> used for a hydrocracking reaction
<HYDROCRACKING> is <CRACKING> of hydrocarbons in the presence of hydrogen
A <HYDROCYCLONE> is a <CYCLONE> and a <CYLINDRICAL VESSEL>, intended to separate a fluid by hydraulic forces
subclasses: HYDROCYCLONE DEOILER

description: A <HYDROCYCLONE DEOILER> is a <HYDROCYCLONE> that is a small cyclone extractor for removing suspended matter from a flowing liquid or separating two fluids with different density by forcing the fluid to flow through a tight conical vortex
<HYDRODEALKYLATING> is the <Activity> of removing methyl groups or larger alkyl groups from hydrocarbons, or to change positions of these groups on the molecule; used to upgrade low-value products
<HYDRODEMETALISING> is the <Activity> of removing of metal from hydrocarbons during oil refining by any of several hydrotreating methods
<HYDRODENITRIFYING> is <DENITRIFYING> hydrocarbons during oil refining by means of hydrotreating
<HYDRODESULPHURISING> is <DEULPHURISING> natural gas and from refined petroleum products by means of a catalytic chemical process
subclasses: DEEP HYDRODESULPHURIZATION

description: A <HYDRODESULPHURIZER REACTOR> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <CHEMICAL REACTOR> used for a desulphurisation reaction

A <HYDRODYNAMIC BEARING> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <BEARING> that conforms to the hydrodynamic lubrication principle, which means that the bearing surfaces are oriented so that relative motion forms an oil wedge, to support the load without shaft-to-bearing contact
subclasses: HYDRODYNAMIC RADIAL BEARING, HYDRODYNAMIC THRUST BEARING, MULTILOBE BEARING

description: A <HYDRODYNAMIC DRIVE> is a <HYDRAULIC TORQUE CONVERTER> utilizing planetary gear trains acting as a oil pump. Throttling the discharge of these pumps creates back pressure and increases the drive torque to the sun gear
A <HYDRODYNAMIC RADIAL BEARING> is a <HYDRODYNAMIC BEARING> and a <RADIAL BEARING> that is designed to support a shaft or rotor in radial direction and to take up radial load

A <HYDRODYNAMIC THRUST BEARING> is a <HYDRODYNAMIC BEARING> and a <THRUST BEARING> that is designed to accommodate for any residual axial load within any rotating equipment design under all possible operating conditions
subclasses: TAPERED LAND THRUST BEARING

description: A <HYDROELECTRIC POWER STATION> is a <POWER STATION> in which the gravitational energy of water is converted into electricity
subclasses: PONDAGE POWER STATION, PUMPED STORAGE POWER STATION, RESERVOIR POWER STATION, RUN-OF-RIVER POWER STATION, TIDAL POWER STATION

description: A <HYDROELECTRIC SET> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <GENERATOR SET> consisting of a hydraulic turbine mechanically connected to an electrical generator
subclasses: BULB-TYPE UNIT

description: <HYDROFINING> is the <Activity> of chemical process for improving the quality of gasoline and other petroleum products by treating with hydrogen in the presence of a catalyst at a temperature below that at which decomposition takes place
<HYDROFLUORIC ACID CORROSION> is an <ACIDIC CORROSION> caused by contact with hydrofluoric acid, which is  a solution of hydrogen fluoride (HF) in water

<HYDROFORMING> is the <Activity> of reforming high-octane gasoline or aromatic hydrocarbons (as toluenes, xylenes) by dehydrogenation and aromatisation of petroleum naphtas. Typically containing a high ratio of naphtenes in a stream of added hydrogen and in the presence of a catalyst

<HYDROFORMYLATION> is the <Activity> of chemical process by the addition of a hydrogen atom and a formyl group to the molecule of a compound containing a double bond by reaction with hydrogen and carbon monoxide, the chief product being one or more aldehydes
A <HYDROGEN> is an <Atom> and a <CHEMICAL ELEMENT> with chemical symbol H and atomic number 1. With an atomic weight of 1.00794 u, hydrogen is the lightest element on the periodic table
A <HYDROGEN COMPOUND> is a <Compound> gas in which the main component is hydrogen
A <HYDROGEN PARTIAL PRESSURE> is a <PARTIAL PRESSURE OF SUBSTANCE B> where substance B is <HYDROGEN>

A <HYDROGEN PROBE> is a <CORROSION MEASURING ELEMENT> designed to measure the permeation rate of atomic hydrogen (H+) (measured as hydrogen gas (H2)) associated with hydrogen-induced cracking. It collects the hydrogen formed on the surface and gives a signal related to amount permeated
<HYDROGEN RECOVERING> is the <Activity> of recovering hydrogen from a mixture, usually by separation
<HYDROGEN SULFIDE> is a <GASEOUS COMPOUND> with the formula H2S. It is a colorless gas with the characteristic foul odor of rotten eggs. It is very poisonous, corrosive, and flammable
A <HYDROGEN SULFIDE COMPOUND> is a <Compound> where the main component is hydrogen sulfide
<HYDROGENATING> is the <Activity> of treating with or exposing to hydrogen, or combining with hydrogen

A <HYDROKINETIC DRIVE> is a <HYDRAULIC TORQUE CONVERTER> utilizing an oil fluid beeing accelerated in an impeller (driving member) and then decelerated as it impinge on the blades of the runner (driven member)

<HYDROLYSING> is the <Activity> of reacting of water in which a bond in the reactant other than water is split, and hydrogen and hydroxyl are added with the formation of two or more new compounds, often with the inclusion of some types of hydration
A <HYDROPHORE SYSTEM> is a <FRESHWATER SUPPLY SYSTEM> used on ships
A <HYDROSTATIC DRIVE> is <FLUID COUPLING> that uses positive displacement hydraulic pumps in conjunction with positive displacement hydraulic motors
A <HYDROSTATIC PRESSURE> is a <PRESSURE> that is exerted by a fluid at equilibrium at a given point within the fluid, due to the force of gravity.
A <HYDROSTATIC TEST PRESSURE> is a <PRESSURE> applied to <PRESSURE VESSEL>s when tested for strength and leaks
subclasses: HYDROSTATIC TEST PRESSURE AT TOP OF VESSEL

uniqueName: HYDROSTATIC TEST PRESSURE AT TOP OF VESSEL
description: A <HYDROSTATIC TEST PRESSURE AT TOP OF VESSEL> is a <HYDROSTATIC TEST PRESSURE> measured at the top of the vessel

A <HYDROSTATIC TEST PRESSURE PERCENT SMYS> is an <IndirectProperty> that refers to a hydrostatic test level defined in terms of pipeline hoop stress as a percentage of Specified Minimum Yield Strength (SMYS)
A <HYDROSTATIC TEST SPECIFICATION> is a <SPECIFICATION> covering the hydrostatic test requirements specified in the manufacturing code or the design code

A <HYDROSTATIC TEST SPECIFICATION DEFINITION> is an <INSPECTION AND TESTING REQUIREMENT SPECIFICATION DEFINITION> that defines the rules for the contents of a specification covering the hydrostatic test requirements specified in the manufacturing code or the design code
superclasses: INSPECTION AND TESTING REQUIREMENT SPECIFICATION DEFINITION

description: A <HYDROSTATIC TEST WEIGHT> is a <TEST WEIGHT> and a <FLUID CONTAINER> filled with water prepared for <PRESSURE> testing
<HYDROSTATIC TESTING> is <PRESSURE TESTING> of strength and tightness by filling with test liquid and increasing the pressure up a level during a period of time given by design specification
A <HYDROSTATICALLY TESTED OBJECT> is a <TESTED OBJECT> that is an instance of <Role> that will be, is, or has been, subjected to <HYDROSTATIC TESTING>
A <HYDROTEST REQUIREMENTS SPECIFICATION> is an <INSPECTION AND TESTING REQUIREMENTS SPECIFICATION> stating the requirement for hydrotest of a product or part of a product

A <HYDROTESTING CAUSES BEGUN HYDROTESTED INDIVIDUAL> is a <CAUSE AND EFFECT> where a member of <HYDROSTATIC TESTING> causes the beginning of a member of a <ClassOfInanimatePhysicalObject> that has the <HYDROSTATICALLY TESTED OBJECT> <Status>
A <HYDROTREATER REACTOR> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <CHEMICAL REACTOR> used for a hydrogen reaction

A <HYDROVISCOUS DRIVE> is a <HYDRAULIC TORQUE CONVERTER> utilizing the variation of shear forces in a oil film. The hydroviscous drive varies its torque capability by varying the film thickness between driving and driven members rotating in oil
<HYPALON> is a <RUBBER> that is a type of synthetic rubber
A <HYPERBOLA> is a <CONIC>; there are two foci such that for the each point in the curve the difference between the distances to each focus is the same
subclasses: CANONICALLY PARAMETERISED HYPERBOLA

description: A <HYPERFINE STRUCTURE QUANTUM NUMBER> is an <IndirectProperty> that refers to a <QUANTUM NUMBER> of an atom describing inclination of the nuclear spin with respect to a quantization axis given by the magnetic field produced by the orbital electrons
A <HYPOID GEAR> is a <GEAR> that has cone shaped gears similar to spiral bevel gears except they transmit motion between non-intersecting shafts.
A <HYPOID GEARBOX> is a <CROSSED AXIS GEARBOX> where the input and output shafts are not intersecting utilizing a pinion and gear with hyperboloid cut gear teeth.
A <HYRAULIC PURGE PIPING SYSTEM> is a <PURGE PIPING SYSTEM> that is a hydraulically controlled piping system that is situated within the frame and distributes purge gas inside the frame
<HYSTERESIS> is the <Activity> of the retardation or lagging of an effect behind the cause of the effect
subclasses: DIELECTRIC HYSTERESIS, MAGNETIC HYSTERESIS

description: A <HYSTERESIS COUPLING> is an <MAGNETIC COUPLING> in which torque is transmitted by forces arising from the resistance to reorientation of established magnetic fields within a ferromagnetic material

A <HYSTERESIS MOTOR> is a <SYNCHRONOUS MOTOR> with a smooth cylindrically shaped member, of magnetic material without a field winding, which starts by virtue of hysteresis losses induced in that member and operates at synchronous speed due to the retentivity of that member
A <HYTIME> is a <ClassOfInformationRepresentation> and <ENCODED DATA> that is hypermedia time based structuring language ISO 10744
An <IAEA SIGN> is a <SAFETY SIGN> that is the standard trefoil radiation warning symbol as standardized by the IAEA
An <I-BEAM STRUCTURE> is a <STRUCTURE(mechanical)> and a <SUPPORT> built from <I-BEAM>s
<ICE> is a <SOLID COMPOUND> which is a solid form of water
An <ICE ANALYSIS REPORT> is an <ANALYSIS REPORT> giving the results of an analysis of <ICE> data
An <ICE ENVIRONMENT STUDY> is an <STUDY REPORT> providing the results of a study on the environment of some occurrence of <ICE>
An <ICE MACHINE> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <FREEZER> that is a stand-alone appliance for making ice
types: ClassOfInanimatePhysicalObject, HEATERS, COOLERS AND HEAT TRANSFER

description: An <ICE SURVEY REPORT> is a <REPORT> describing how, when and where ice data has been collected
An <Identification> is a <RepresentationOfThing> that indicates that the <sign> <PossibleIndividual> is an identifier for the <represented> <Thing>
An <IDENTIFICATION NUMBER> is an <ExpressInteger> and an <IDENTIFIER>
subclasses: ATOMIC NUMBER, COUNTRY NUMBER, FAX NUMBER, INTERNAL INSPECTION RUN NUMBER, PERFORMANCE CURVE NUMBER

uniqueName: IDENTIFICATION OF SAFETY CRITICAL ELEMENTS REPORT
description: An <IDENTIFICATION OF SAFETY CRITICAL ELEMENTS REPORT> is a <REPORT> that lists all safety critical elements (SCE)
An <IDENTIFICATION SYSTEM> is a <ClassOfInformationRepresentation> that defines the rules, language, and format of an identification string
subclasses: ASSET NUMBER IDENTIFICATION SYSTEM, BUILDING IDENTIFICATION SYSTEM, CABLE IDENTIFICATION SYSTEM, CONSTRUCTION AREA IDENTIFICATION SYSTEM, DOCUMENT NUMBERING SYSTEM, PLANT IDENTIFICATION SYSTEM, PROCESS UNIT IDENTIFICATION SYSTEM, ROAD IDENTIFICATION SYSTEM, SERIAL NUMBER IDENTIFICATION SYSTEM, STRUCTURAL FRAMEWORK IDENTIFICATION SYSTEM, TAG NUMBERING SYSTEM

description: An <IDENTIFIER> is a <FunctionalObject>  with the purpose of <IDENTIFYING> something
subclasses: IDENTIFICATION NUMBER, IDENTIFYING STRING, PHYSICAL LABEL

description: <IDENTIFYING> is the <Activity> of establishing the sameness in all that constitutes the objective reality of (a thing)
An <IDENTIFYING STRING> is an <ExpressString> and an <IDENTIFIER> that is a term that is sufficiently unique within a context to identify an object
subclasses: ACCESS CODE, ACTIVITY NUMBER, ACX NUMBER, ADDRESS, ASSET NUMBER, BATCH IDENTIFIER, BUILDING NUMBER, CABLE NUMBER, CARGO NUMBER, CAS REGISTRY NUMBER, CHEMICAL IDENTIFIER, COLOUR CODE, COMPANY CODE, CONCATENATED CODE, CONSTRUCTION AREA NUMBER, CONTRACT NUMBER, COUNTRY CODE, CYLINDER IDENTIFIER, DAMAGE CONTROL CODE, DESIGN FOLDER CODE, DISCIPLINE CODE, DOCUMENT NUMBER, DOCUMENT REVISION CODE, DOCUMENT REVISION NUMBER, DRILL PERMIT IDENTIFIER, DRIVE END BEARING TYPE CODE, ELECTRIC ROTATING MACHINE COOLING METHOD CODE, EMPLOYEE NUMBER, EQUIPMENT ORIGIN CODE, EQUIPMENT REMOVAL NEED INDICATOR, FAULT BLOCK IDENTIFIER, FIELD JOINT NUMBER, FIELD WELD NUMBER, FLOWLINE IDENTIFIER, FORMATION IDENTIFIER, GIRTH WELD IDENTIFIER, HAZARDOUS AREA ZONE CODE, HEAT TRACING SYSTEM NUMBER, HOUSE NUMBER, INSPECTION REPORT NUMBER, INSTRUMENT TAG, INSULATION TAG, INTENDED SERVICE CODE, ITEM NUMBER, JOB IDENTIFIER, LABEL TEXT, LANGUAGE CODE, LINE NUMBER, LOCATION CODE, LOGISTIC REPORT CODE, LUBRICATION CODE, MAINTENANCE NUMBER, MANUFACTURER ORDER IDENTIFIER, MANUFACTURERS IDENTIFIER OF DRILL BIT, MATERIAL DATA SHEET IDENTIFICATION CODE, MATERIAL SUBCODE, MESSAGE IDENTIFIER, METAL-LOSS CLUSTER NUMBER, MODEL NUMBER, NAME, NOZZLE NUMBER, ORDER NUMBER, ORGANIZATION CODE, PACKAGE IDENTIFIER, PAGE NUMBER, PART CRITICALITY CODE, PBS CODE, POST CODE, POST OFFICE BOX NUMBER ID, PROJECT CODE, PURCHASE ORDER LINE ITEM NUMBER, PURCHASE ORDER NUMBER, QUOTATION NUMBER, RDFS LABEL, RFQ IDENTIFIER, ROAD NUMBER, SEQUENCE NUMBER, SERIAL NUMBER, SOCIAL SECURITY NUMBER (US), SPEED/TORQUE CURVE NUMBER, STARTING METHOD CODE, STREAM NUMBER, STRUCTURAL FRAMEWORK NUMBER, SUPPORT NUMBER, SYSTEM NUMBER, TAG NUMBER, WBS CODE, WINDING INSULATION CODE, WIRE TAG, WORK ORDER IDENTIFIER, XML END TAG, XML START TAG

description: An <IDLER GEAR> is a <GEAR> rotor running free (not driven by timing gear).
An <IDLER SHAFT> is a <SHAFT> that locates gears within a gear box, but does not transmit power.
<IDLING> is the <Activity> of running or causing to run disconnected or unloaded so that power is not used for external or useful work
An <IDR> is a <CURRENCY> called 'Rupiah' and used in INDONESIA
<IFA> is an <InformationRepresentation>, typed as <STATUS CODE>, denoting the <Status> <ISSUED FOR APPROVAL>
An <IFA EVENT> is an <Event> at which an <ISSUED FOR APPROVAL> <Status> takes place
<IFC> is an <InformationRepresentation>, typed as <STATUS CODE>, denoting the <Status> <ISSUED FOR CONSTRUCTION>
An <IFC EVENT> is an <Event> at which an <ISSUED FOR CONSTRUCTION> <Status> takes place
<IFD> is an <InformationRepresentation>, typed as <STATUS CODE>, denoting the <Status> <ISSUED FOR DESIGN>
<IFH> is an <InformationRepresentation>, typed as <STATUS CODE>, denoting the <Status> <ISSUED FOR HAZOP>
An <IFH EVENT> is an <Event> at which an <ISSUED FOR HAZOP> <Status> takes place
<IFI> is an <InformationRepresentation>, typed as <STATUS CODE>, denoting the <Status> <ISSUED FOR INFORMATION>
An <IFI EVENT> is an <Event> at which an <ISSUED FOR  INFORMATION> <status> takes place
<IFP> is an <InformationRepresentation>, typed as <STATUS CODE>, denoting the <Status> <ISSUED FOR PURCHASE>
An <IFP EVENT> is an <Event> at which an <ISSUED FOR PURCHASE> <Status> takes place
<IFQ> is an <InformationRepresentation>, typed as <STATUS CODE>, denoting the <Status>  <ISSUED FOR QUOTATION>
An <IFQ EVENT> is an <Event> at which an <ISSUED FOR QUOTATION> <Status> takes place
<IFR> is an <InformationRepresentation>, typed as <STATUS CODE>, denoting the <Status> <ISSUED FOR REVIEW>

A <LEVEL GAUGE> is a <LEVEL MEASURING INSTRUMENT> and a <PROCESS GAUGE> using a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT>, that is intended to display a representation of a measured level
subclasses: LEVEL GAUGE GLASS, MAGNETIC LEVEL GAUGE

description: A <LEVEL GAUGE GLASS> is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and a <LEVEL GAUGE> that is a glass tubular device or vertical cylindrical device, often graduated, that indicates the level or amount of liquid in a tank or vessel
A <LEVEL GAUGE NOZZLE> is an <INSTRUMENT NOZZLE> intended for mounting a level gauge.
A <LEVEL MEASURING CHAMBER> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <CONTAINER> that creates a place for representative level measurement.
A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT> is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and a <MEASURING ELEMENT> for measuring a <LIQUID LEVEL>
subclasses: LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - DISPLACER, LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - ELECTRIC PROPERTY, LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - FLOAT, LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - GRAVIMETRIC, LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - HYDROSTATIC PRESSURE, LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - LASER, LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - MECHANICAL, LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - NUCLEAR, LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - OPTICAL, LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - REFRACTIVE, LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - RESISTANCE TAPE, LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - THERMAL CONDUCTIVITY, LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - WAVE

uniqueName: LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - AIR BUBBLER SYSTEM
description: A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - AIR BUBBLER SYSTEM> is a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - PRESSURE> that uses a tube with an opening below the surface of the liquid level. A fixed flow of air is passed through the tube. Pressure in the tube is proportional to the depth (and density) of the liquid over the outlet of the tube

A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - CAPACITANCE> is a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - ELECTRIC PROPERTY> that senses the presence of a wide variety of solids, aqueous and organic liquids, and slurries. The technique is frequently referred to as RF for the radio frequency signals applied to the capacitance circuit

A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - CONDUCTANCE> is a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - ELECTRIC PROPERTY> that uses a low-voltage, current-limited power source applied across separate electrodes. The power supply is matched to the conductivity of the liquid, with higher voltage versions designed to operate in less conductive (higher resistance) mediums. A conductive liquid contacting both the longest probe (common) and a shorter probe (return) completes a conductive circuit
A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - CONTINUOUS-WAVE RADAR> is a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - FREE-SPACE RADAR> that uses a continuous radar wave to measure level

A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE> is a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - HYDROSTATIC PRESSURE> that is measuring liquid level by sensing pressure difference between two points, e.g. the hydrostatic pressure at the bottom of a tank to the atmosphere pressure
A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - DISPLACER> is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT> that uses the buoyancy force from a suspended displacer that is immersed in the liquid

A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - ELECTRIC PROPERTY> is an <ELECTRICAL APPARATUS> and an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT> that uses the electric properties of a process material to measure its level
superclasses: ELECTRICAL APPARATUS, INSTRUMENTATION ITEM, LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT
subclasses: LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - CAPACITANCE, LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - CONDUCTANCE, LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - RF ADMITTANCE

description: A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - FLOAT> is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT> that involves the actuation of a mechanical switch actuated by a float
subclasses: LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - FLOAT - MAGNET, LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - FLOAT - RESISTIVE CHAIN, LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - MAGNETORESISTIVE FLOAT, LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - MAGNETOSTRICTIVE, LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - MAGNETOSTRICTIVE FLOAT, LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - TILTED FLOAT

description: A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - FLOAT - MAGNET> is a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - FLOAT> that uses a magnet and resistors to determine the position of the float

uniqueName: LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - FLOAT - RESISTIVE CHAIN
description: A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - FLOAT - RESISTIVE CHAIN> is a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - FLOAT> where a permanent magnet, sealed inside a float, moves up and down a stem in which closely spaced switches and resistors are sealed. When the switches are closed, the resistance is summed and converted to current or voltage signals that are proportional to the level of the liquid
A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - FREE-SPACE RADAR> is a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - WAVE> that uses the travelling time of a radar beam to measure level
subclasses: LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - CONTINUOUS-WAVE RADAR, LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - PULSED-WAVE RADAR

description: A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - GAMMA RAY> is a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - WAVE> that measures level by the attenuation of gamma rays passing through a process vessel. The technique is used to regulate the level of molten steel in a continuous casting process of steelmaking

A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - GRAVIMETRIC> is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT> that measures <LIQUID LEVEL> on the basis of the <WEIGHT> of the <LIQUID COMPOUNG> contained by the <VESSEL>

A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - GUIDED-WAVE RADAR> is a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - WAVE> that emits a wave that is guided by a rod, cable or rope to the surface of process material and uses the time of flight of the reflected wave to measure level

A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - HYDROSTATIC PRESSURE> is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT> that is a submersible or externally mounted pressure sensor that senses increasing pressure with depth
subclasses: LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE, LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - PRESSURE

description: A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - IMMERSION> is a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - PRESSURE> the sensing element of which is immersed in the liquid to be measured
A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - LASER> is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT> that uses the travelling time of a laser beam to measure level

A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - MAGNETORESISTIVE FLOAT> is a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - FLOAT> where a permanent magnet pair is sealed inside the float arm pivot. As the float moves up the motion and location are transmitted as the angular position of the magnetic field
A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - MAGNETOSTRICTIVE> is a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - FLOAT> that uses the magnetostrictive effect to determine the position of the float

A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - MAGNETOSTRICTIVE FLOAT> is a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - FLOAT> where a permanent magnet, sealed inside a float, travels up and down a stem in which a magnetostrictive wire is sealed. For high-accuracy, continuous level measurement of a wide variety of liquids
A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - MECHANICAL> is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT> that uses mechanical means to measure level
subclasses: LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - PLUMB BOB, LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - ROTATING PADDLE, LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - SERVO, LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - VIBRATING

description: A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - NUCLEAR> is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and  a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT> that uses the absorption of gamma radiation by process material to measure level

A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - OPTICAL> is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and  a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT> that uses the transmission, reflection or refraction of light by the process material to measure level
subclasses: LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - OPTICAL INFRARED, LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - OPTICAL LASER

description: A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - OPTICAL INFRARED> is a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - OPTICAL> that is used for point level sensing of sediments, liquids with suspended solids, and liquid-liquid interfaces. These sensors sense the decrease or change in transmission of infrared light emitted from an infrared diode (LED)

A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - OPTICAL LASER> is a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - OPTICAL> that involves the use of a laser. Laser light reflects off most solid, liquid surfaces. The time of flight can be measured with precise timing circuitry, to determine the range or distance of the surface from the sensor
subclasses: LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - OPTICAL REFLECTION, LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - OPTICAL REFRACTION

description: A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - OPTICAL REFLECTION> is a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - OPTICAL LASER> that uses the principle of reflection to measure level

A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - OPTICAL REFRACTION> is a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - OPTICAL LASER> that uses the difference between the refractive index of the process fluid and the material of the sensing element to measure level
A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - PLUMB BOB> is a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - MECHANICAL> that uses a wire or tape with a body as sensing element to measure level
A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - PRESSURE> is a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - HYDROSTATIC PRESSURE> that uses gauge pressure to measure level
subclasses: LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - AIR BUBBLER SYSTEM, LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - IMMERSION

description: A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - PULSED MICROWAVE> is a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - WAVE> that using a Pulsed Reflectometry signal processing technique
A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - PULSED-WAVE RADAR> is a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - FREE-SPACE RADAR> that uses a pulsed radar wave to measure level

A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - REFRACTIVE> is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT> that uses the difference between the refractive index of the process fluid and the material of the sensing element to measure level

A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - RESISTANCE TAPE> is a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT> that is a resistive tape that stretches the entire height of the vessel, and contact is made between two resistive wires by the head pressure against the submerged length of the tape

A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - RF ADMITTANCE> is a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - ELECTRIC PROPERTY> that uses a rod probe and RF source to measures the change in admittance (a measure of how easily a circuit will allow a current to flow). When the level changes around the probe, a corresponding change in the di-electric is observed. This changes the admittance of this imperfect capacitor and this change is measured to detect change of level

A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - ROTATING PADDLE> is a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - MECHANICAL> that is an established technique for bulk solid point level indication. It uses a low-speed gear motor that rotates a paddle wheel. When the paddle is stalled by solid materials, the motor is rotated on its shaft by its own torque until a flange mounted on the motor contacts a mechanical switch
A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - SERVO> is a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - MECHANICAL> that uses a float and a wire fed by a servo motor to measure level

uniqueName: LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - SINGLE PROBE VIBRATING
description: A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - SINGLE PROBE VIBRATING> is a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - VIBRATING> for bulk powder level measurement. It is not affected by dust, static-charge build-up from dielectric powders, or changes in conductivity, temperature, pressure, humidity or moisture content. Since only one sensing element contacts the powder, bridging between two probe elements is eliminated and media build-up is minimized

A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - TDR MICROWAVE> is a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - WAVE> using a Time-Domain Reflectometry signal processing technique which is a measurement of time of flight divided by the speed of light
A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - THERMAL CONDUCTIVITY> is a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT> when inserted in the liquid
A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - TILTED FLOAT> is a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - FLOAT> that uses the tilting of the float

uniqueName: LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - TUNING FORK VIBRATING
description: A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - TUNING FORK VIBRATING> is a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - VIBRATING> for bulk powder level measurement. It is not affected by dust, static-charge build-up from dielectric powders, or changes in conductivity, temperature, pressure, humidity or moisture content, but it is prone to material buildup between the tines

A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - ULTRASONIC> is a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - WAVE> that is used for non-contact level sensing of liquids and bulk solids. It emits high frequency (20 kHz to 200 kHz) acoustic waves that are reflected back to and detected by the emitting transducer. Ultrasonic sensors can be designed to provide point level control, continuous monitoring or both
A <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - VIBRATING> is a <LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - MECHANICAL> that is vibrating to measure level
subclasses: LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - SINGLE PROBE VIBRATING, LEVEL MEASURING ELEMENT - TUNING FORK VIBRATING

A <LUMINANCE> is a <Property> that is the intensity of light emitted at a point on a <SURFACE> and in a given direction, calculates as  L_v = dI_v/dA where dI_v is the luminous intensity of an element of A <SURFACE> with A <AREA> dA of the orthogonal projection of this element on a plane perpendicular to the given direction
A <LUMINOUS ABSORPTANCE> is a <RATIO> of the absorbed <LUMINOUS FLUX>  Phi_v,a to the  <LUMINOUS FLUX> Phi_v,m of the incident radiation, thus alpha_v = Phi_v,a / Phi_v,m

A <LUMINOUS EFFICACY Of RADIATION> is a <Property> that, for a specified photometric condition, is the quotient of luminous flux and the corresponding radiant flux for a specified photometric condition; expressed as K=Φv/Φe, where Φv is luminous flux and Φe is radiant flux. (IEV ref 845-21-090)
<LUMINOUS EFFICIENCY> is an <EFFICIENCY> of <RADIATION>  compared to the Maximum possible efficiency as defined in ISO 80000-7 (2008) 7-30
A <LUMINOUS EXITANCE> is a <Property> that is a measure of the ability of a surface to emit light expressed as the luminous flux per unit area at a specified point on the surface
A <LUMINOUS EXPOSURE SCALE> is a <Scale> for light exposure

A <LUMINOUS FLUX> is a <Property> that is the quantity of an <ENERGY> of the light emitted per second in all directions calculated as  Phi_v = K_m.integral[0, infinity](Phi_lambda(lambda) .V(lambda) d.lambda where K_m is the maximum spectral luminous efficacy, Phi_lambda(lambda) is the spectral radiant flux, V(lambda) is the spectral <LUMINOUS EFFICIENCY> and lambda is the wavelength

A <LUMINOUS INTENSITY> is a <Property> that is a measure of the wavelength-weighted power emitted by a light source in a particular direction per unit solid angle, based on the luminosity function, a standardized model of the sensitivity of the human eye
A <LUMINOUS REFLECTANCE> is a <RATIO> of the reflected <LUMINOUS FLUX> Phi_v,r to a <LUMINOUS FLUX> Phi_v,m of the incident radiation, thus rho_v = Phi_v,r / Phi_v,m
A <LUMINOUS TRANSMITTANCE> is a <RATIO> of the transmitted <LUMINOUS FLUX> Phi_v,t to a <LUMINOUS FLUX> Phi_v,m of the incident radiation, thus tau_v = Phi_v,t / Phi_v,m

A <LUX> is a <PropertyQuantification> between an <ILLUMINANCE> and a <NUMBER SPACE OF 0 TO INF>
A <LYD> is a <CURRENCY> called &amp;#39;Libyan Dinar&amp;#39; and used in LIBYA
A <MACH NUMBER> is a <RATIO> of a <SPEED> of a body to a <SPEED> of sound in the surrounding medium. Calculated as   Ma = v/c where v is <SPEED> and c is <SPEED> sound

A <MAGNETIC CORE> is a <MACHINE COMPONENT> that is the bar or cylinder of soft iron forming the central part of an electro-magnet, or of an induction-coil

A <MAGNETIC FIELD STRENGTH> is a <Property> that is the amount of <MAGNETIC FLUX> in a unit area perpendicular to the direction of magnetic flow, calculated as  H = B / mju_0 - M where B is  <MAGNETIC FLUX DENSITY>, mju_0 is the magnetic constant, and M is <MAGNETIZATION>

description: A <MAGNETIC POLARIZATION> is a <VECTOR> field that expresses the density of permanent or induced magnetic dipole moments in a magnetic material.

subclasses: MAGNETOMOTIVE FORCE

description: A <MAGNETIC QUANTUM NUMBER> is a <PhysicalObject> that is the third in a set of atomic quantum numbers related to the z-component l_z, j_z or s_z of the orbital, total or spin angular momentum
A <MAGNETIC RELUCTANCE PICKUP> is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and a <PICKUP COIL> using the <MAGNETIC RELUCTANCE> principle (Used in turbine flow meters.)

A <MAGNETIC REYNOLDS NUMBER> is a <Property> that that indicates the dynamic behaviour of a plasma, and is used to determine whether or not a fluid flow will smooth out or become turbulent, as defined  ISO 80000-11 (2008) 11-8.1

A <MAGNETIC SHUNT> is a <MACHINE COMPONENT> that is a device of high-permeability material which is placed in parallel with part of a magnetic circuit to divert flux from that part

A <MAGNETIC SUSCEPTIBILITY> is a dimensionless <Property> that indicates the degree of <MAGNETIZATION> of a material in response to an applied magnetic field M = kappa.H where M is <MAGNETIZATION> and H is <MAGNETIC FIELD STRENGTH>

A <MAGNETIC TENSION> is a <FORCE> that gives rise to an equilibrium in a physical system, and that acts to straighten bent magnetic field lines.  It is calculated as  U_m = integral^r_b _r_a (H.dr) where H is <MAGNETIC FIELD STRENGTH> and r is position vector along a given curve C from point a to point b

A <MAGNETIC VECTOR POTENTIAL> is a <VECTOR> field that serves as the potential for the magnetic field. Its curl is the magnetic field. It is preferred when working with the Lagrangian in classical mechanics and quantum mechanics
A <MAGNETICALLY COUPLED PUMP> is a <SEALLESS CENTRIFUGAL PUMP> where the driver is coupled to the pump by a drive magnet that eliminates any shaft sealing required by the pump
A <MAGNETO-HYDRO-DYNAMIC THERMAL POWER STATION> is a <THERMAL POWER STATION> generating electricity by means of an electromagnetic field acting on a plasma stream.
A <MAGNETOMETER> is a <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and a <MEASURING INSTRUMENT> that is intended to measure the value of a magnetic flux density in a given direction

A <MAGNETOMOTIVE FORCE> is a <MAGNETIC PRESSURE> that sets up the <MAGNETIC FLUX> in a magnetic circuit. it is calculated as   F_m = integral_C(H.dr) where H is <MAGNETIC FIELD STRENGTH> and r is position vector along a closed curve C

<MAINTAINED> is an <INDIVIDUAL WITH A STATUS> of being or having been subjected to a maintenance activity
A <MAINTAINER> is a <PERFORMER> that is a performing <Role> in the <Activity> of <MAINTAINING>

subclasses: BOILER MAINTENANCE, CONDITION-BASED MAINTENANCE, CORRECTIVE MAINTENANCE, DRILLING RIG MAINTENANCE, IN-LINE MAINTENANCE, PREVENTIVE MAINTENANCE, SHOP MAINTENANCE, TROUBLESHOOTING

description: <MAINTENANCE SUPPORT> is the <Activity> of supporting maintenance activities

<MAKING UP> is the <Activity> of getting into condition for

uniqueName: MASS FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - SONIC NOZZLE
description: A <MASS FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - SONIC NOZZLE> is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and a <MASS FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT> that is operated by pressurizing the inlet of a venturi or evacuating its outlet in order to achieve an Inlet to Outlet pressure ratio of 1.4 to 1 or greater. This ratio maintains the Nozzle in a &amp;amp;amp;quot;choked&amp;amp;amp;quot; or &amp;amp;amp;quot;sonic&amp;amp;amp;quot; state. In this state, only the upstream pressure and temperature influence the flow rate of gas through the Nozzle. The flow rate through the Nozzle becomes nearly a linear function of the inlet pressure which increases the thereby doubling the flow rate of gas
superclasses: INSTRUMENTATION ITEM, MASS FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT

description: A <MASS FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - THERMAL> is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and a <MASS FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT> that uses combinations of heated elements and temperature sensors to measure the difference between static and flowing heat transfer to a fluid and infer its flow with a knowledge of the fluids specific heat and density. The fluid temperature is also measured and compensated for. If the density and specific heat characteristics of the fluid are constant, the meter can provide a direct mass flow readout, and does not need any additional pressure temperature compensation over their specified range
superclasses: INSTRUMENTATION ITEM, MASS FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT

uniqueName: MECHANICAL SEAL AUTOMATIC REFILLING LUBRICATION SYSTEM
description: A <MECHANICAL SEAL AUTOMATIC REFILLING LUBRICATION SYSTEM> is a <MECHANICAL SEAL CLOSED CIRCUIT LIQUID LUBRICATION SYSTEM> where the buffer fluid is circulated and cooled in a loop outside the fluid tank. The pressurisation and leakage compensation is taken care of by an electric or pneumatic driven pump with pressure control valve for manual regulation of buffer fluid pressure. Should the pump be swithed off, the pressure will be maintained for a limited time by an accumulator.
superclasses: MECHANICAL SEAL CLOSED CIRCUIT LIQUID LUBRICATION SYSTEM

uniqueName: MECHANICAL SEAL CLOSED CIRCUIT LIQUID LUBRICATION SYSTEM
description: A <MECHANICAL SEAL CLOSED CIRCUIT LIQUID LUBRICATION SYSTEM> is a <MECHANICAL SEAL LIQUID LUBRICATION SYSTEM> where all components are kept under the same pressure. The pressure is applied by means of nitrogen, by the process medium pressure or via a refill system.
subclasses: MECHANICAL SEAL AUTOMATIC REFILLING LUBRICATION SYSTEM, MECHANICAL SEAL CLOSED LOOP LUBRICATION SYSTEM, MECHANICAL SEAL DEAD END LUBRICATION SYSTEM, MECHANICAL SEAL EXTERNAL SOURCE LUBRICATION SYSTEM, MECHANICAL SEAL PRESSURE BOOSTER LUBRICATION SYSTEM, MECHANICAL SEAL QUENCH FLUID LUBRICATION SYSTEM, MECHANICAL SEAL THERMOSIPHON LUBRICATION SYSTEM

uniqueName: MECHANICAL SEAL CLOSED LOOP LUBRICATION SYSTEM
description: A <MECHANICAL SEAL CLOSED LOOP LUBRICATION SYSTEM> is a <MECHANICAL SEAL CLOSED CIRCUIT LIQUID LUBRICATION SYSTEM> where the buffer fluid is circulated through a cooler by a pumping ring in the seal chamber. Possible leakage compensation is taken care of by manual refilling.
superclasses: MECHANICAL SEAL CLOSED CIRCUIT LIQUID LUBRICATION SYSTEM

uniqueName: MECHANICAL SEAL DEAD END LUBRICATION SYSTEM
description: A <MECHANICAL SEAL DEAD END LUBRICATION SYSTEM> is a <MECHANICAL SEAL CLOSED CIRCUIT LIQUID LUBRICATION SYSTEM> where the buffer fluid is supplied to the seal chamber inlet only. The seal chamber outlet is plugged.
superclasses: MECHANICAL SEAL CLOSED CIRCUIT LIQUID LUBRICATION SYSTEM

uniqueName: MECHANICAL SEAL EXTERNAL SOURCE LUBRICATION SYSTEM
description: A <MECHANICAL SEAL EXTERNAL SOURCE LUBRICATION SYSTEM> is a <MECHANICAL SEAL CLOSED CIRCUIT LIQUID LUBRICATION SYSTEM> where clean buffer fluid is circulated through the seal chamber by an external source. The buffer fluid pressure is greater than the process fluid pressure. Typically it can be water from the freshwater supply system.
superclasses: MECHANICAL SEAL CLOSED CIRCUIT LIQUID LUBRICATION SYSTEM

description: A <MECHANICAL SEAL GAS LUBRICATION SYSTEM> is a <MECHANICAL SEAL LUBRICATION SYSTEM> providing gas (N2 or air) to dry gas seals (DGS) arrangements.
A <MECHANICAL SEAL LIQUID LUBRICATION SYSTEM> is a <MECHANICAL SEAL LUBRICATION SYSTEM> providing buffer fluid to a pressurized dual arrangements.
subclasses: MECHANICAL SEAL CLOSED CIRCUIT LIQUID LUBRICATION SYSTEM, MECHANICAL SEAL OPEN CIRCUIT LIQUID LUBRICATION SYSTEM

description: A <MECHANICAL SEAL LUBRICATION SYSTEM> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <LUBRICATION SYSTEM> which provides lubrication and/or buffer fluid to a mechanical seal arrangement
subclasses: MECHANICAL SEAL GAS LUBRICATION SYSTEM, MECHANICAL SEAL LIQUID LUBRICATION SYSTEM, MECHANICAL SEAL PRODUCT LUBRICATION SYSTEM

uniqueName: MECHANICAL SEAL OPEN CIRCUIT LIQUID LUBRICATION SYSTEM
description: A <MECHANICAL SEAL OPEN CIRCUIT LIQUID LUBRICATION SYSTEM> is a <MECHANICAL SEAL LIQUID LUBRICATION SYSTEM> where the circulation and pressurization take place through a single buffer fluid system. After each circuit the buffer fluid is relieved and collected in a pressureless tank.

uniqueName: MECHANICAL SEAL PRESSURE BOOSTER LUBRICATION SYSTEM
description: A <MECHANICAL SEAL PRESSURE BOOSTER LUBRICATION SYSTEM> is a <MECHANICAL SEAL CLOSED CIRCUIT LIQUID LUBRICATION SYSTEM> where the buffer fluid flows via a rising pipe into a vessel where it is cooled. The vessel is pressurized by means of a piston activated by the process medium pressure. This system is often used for double and tandem mechanical seal applications.
superclasses: MECHANICAL SEAL CLOSED CIRCUIT LIQUID LUBRICATION SYSTEM

description: A <MECHANICAL SEAL PRODUCT LUBRICATION SYSTEM> is a <MECHANICAL SEAL LUBRICATION SYSTEM> providing product lubrication to single mechanical seal arrangements.
subclasses: API 682 SEAL PIPING PLAN

uniqueName: MECHANICAL SEAL QUENCH FLUID LUBRICATION SYSTEM
description: A <MECHANICAL SEAL QUENCH FLUID LUBRICATION SYSTEM> is a <MECHANICAL SEAL CLOSED CIRCUIT LIQUID LUBRICATION SYSTEM> acting as a reservoir, supplying single or tandem mechanical seals. The exchange of fluid takes place by thermosiphon principle or by forced circulation e.g. with a pumping ring.
superclasses: MECHANICAL SEAL CLOSED CIRCUIT LIQUID LUBRICATION SYSTEM

description: A <MECHANICAL SEAL THERMOSIPHON LUBRICATION SYSTEM> is a <MECHANICAL SEAL CLOSED CIRCUIT LIQUID LUBRICATION SYSTEM> where the buffer fluid flows via a rising pipe into a vessel where it is cooled. The vessel is pressurized with air or nitrogen. This system is often used for double and tandem mechanical seal applications.
superclasses: MECHANICAL SEAL CLOSED CIRCUIT LIQUID LUBRICATION SYSTEM

description: <MECHANICAL SEPARATION> is <SEPARATING(physical)>(physical) using mechanical means

A <MOLAR FLOW RATE> is a <FLOW RATE> that is a measure of the number of moles of a substance passing through a given point in a system per unit of time. It quantifies the rate at which a particular chemical species is flowing through a process or a defined area. It is calculated by multiplying the <VOLUME FLOW RATE> of the substance by its <MOLAR CONCENTRATION>  at that point in the system
A <MOLAR FLOW RATE SCALE> is a <Scale> for molar flow rate

The <MOLAR GAS CONSTANT R> is a <Property> that is a fundamental physical constant which appears in a large number of fundamental equations in the physical sciences, such as the ideal gas law and other equations of state and the Nernst equation. It is equivalent to the the Boltzmann constant (kB) times Avogadro's constant (N): R = kBNA.
A <MOLAR HEAT CAPACITY> is a <RATIO> of a <HEAT CAPACITY> divided by the amount of substance
A <MOLAR MASS> of a pure sample is a <RATIO> of a <MASS> divided by amount of substance, expressed by M = m/n where m is <MASS> and n is the amount of substance
A <MOLAR MASS SCALE> is a <Scale> for molar mass

A <MOLAR OPTICAL ROTATORY POWER> is a <Property> expressed by alpha_n = alpha.A/n where alpha is the angle of optical rotation, and n is the amountof substance of the optically active component in the path of a linearly polarized light beam of a cross-sectional area A
A <MOLAR QUANTITY SCALE> is a <Scale> for amount of substance

A <MOLAR SPECIFIC ENERGY> is a <Property> that is an <ENERGY> per unit <MOLE>. It represents the total energy contained within a mole of a substance, which can be released or utilized in chemical reactions or other processes involving molecular or atomic interactions
A <MOLAR THERMODYNAMIC ENERGY> is a <RATIO> expressed by U_m = U / n where U is internal <ENERGY> and n is the amount of substance
A <MOLAR VOLUME> for a pure sample is a <RATIO> expressed by V_m = V/n where V is volume and n is the amount of substance
A <MOLAR VOLUME SCALE> is a <Scale> for concentration volume per mole

An <ORTHOGONAL COORDINATE SYSTEM> is a <FunctionalMapping> that is defined by an ordered pair of perpendicular lines (axes), a single unit of length for both axes, and an orientation for each axis. The point where the axes meet is taken as the origin for both, thus turning each axis into a number line. For any point P, a line is drawn through P perpendicular to each axis, and the position where it meets the axis is interpreted as a number. The two numbers, in that chosen order, are the Cartesian coordinates of P

Defined in ISO 80000-9 (2009) 9-29.2

description: <OWL 2 EL> is a syntactic subset of <OWL 2> that enables polynomial time algorithms for all the standard reasoning tasks; it is particularly suitable for applications where very large ontologies are needed, and where expressive power can be traded for performance guarantees

<OWL 2 RL> is a syntactic subset of <OWL 2> that enables the implementation of polynomial time reasoning algorithms using rule-extended database technologies operating directly on RDF triples; it is particularly suitable for applications where relatively lightweight ontologies are used to organize large numbers of individuals and where it is useful or necessary to operate directly on data in the form of RDF triples.

A <PH ANALYSER> is a <PROCESS ANALYSER> intended to determine the concentration of free hydrogen-ions in an aqueous solution, indicating its acidity or basicity expressed as <pH>, thereby using a <PH MEASURING ELEMENT> and a <PH TRANSMITTER>

<PHASE SEGREGATED PROTECTING> is <ELECTRICAL PROTECTING>, generally <UNIT PROTECTING>s, that is phase selective

A <PHASE-TO-PHASE CLEARANCE> is an <IndirectProperty> that refers to a <CLEARANCE> that is the minimum <DISTANCE> between live parts of two adjacent phases taking into account all operating conditions

A <PHOTON> is a <SubAtomicParticle> that has a single quantum unit of electromagnetic energy. It is regarded as a discrete particle having zero mass, no electric charge, and an indefinitely long lifetime

The <PHOTON EXITANCE> is a <Property> that is, for a point on a <SURFACE>, the <PHOTON FLUX> leaving an element of the <SURFACE>, divided by the <AREA> of that element. Defined in ISO 80000-7 (2008) 7-5

The <PHOTON EXPOSURE> is a <Property> that is a time integral of photon irradiance E_p during the <DURATION> delta t, thus H_p, thus H_p =integral[0, delta t](E_p. dt). Defined in ISO 80000-7 (2008) 7-55

The <PHOTON FLUX> is a <Property> that is a quotient of the number dN_p of protons emitted, transmitted, or received in a <TIME> interval, by its <DURATION> dt, thus Phi_p = dN_p / dt. Defined in ISO 80000-7 (2008) 7-50

The <PHOTON INTENSITY> is a <Property> that is a measure of the Intensity of the <INTENSITY> of exposure to <LIGHT> in a given direction from a source in an elementary <CONE> containing the given <DIRECTION, divided by A <SOLID ANGLE> as defined in ISO 80000-7 (2008) 7-51

The <PHOTON IRRADIANCE> is a <Property> that is a measure of the the <PHOTON FLUX>  incident on an element of the <SURFACE>, divided by the <AREA> of that element as defined in ISO 80000-7 (2008) 7-54

A <PHOTON LUMINANCE> is a <Property> that is, at a point on a surfact and in a given direction, the proton intensity dI_p of an element of that surface, divided by an <AREA> dA of the orthogonal projection of this element on a plane perpendicular to the given direction, thus L_p = dI_p /dA. Defined in ISO 80000-7 (2008) 7-52

The <PHOTON NUMBER> is a <COUNT> of the number of photons detected in a given <TIME>. It may be calculated for a monochromatic radiation of <FREQUENCY)> nu  as N_p = Q/(h.nu) where Q is radiant energy,  h is the <PLANCK CONSTANT> . Defined in ISO 80000-7 (2008) 7-49
A <PHOTOTRANSISTOR> is a <TRANSISTOR> that responds to incident light by generating and amplifying an electric current.
A <PHOTOVOLTAIC CELL> is a <PHOTOCELL> and a <PHOTOVOLTAIC DEVICE> that is the smallest voltage generating part from which other photovoltaic devices are assembled

<PIPELINE PRECOMMISSIONING CLEANING> is <PIPELINE CLEANING> internally prior to or as part of the commissioning activity
<PIPELINE PREINSPECTION CLEANING> is <PIPELINE CLEANING> that is an internal cleaning of a pipeline prior to an inspection
<PIPELINE PRELAY SURVEYING> is <SURVEYING> to gather data about the pipeline environment immediately in advance of its construction - generally this is a rolling survey ahead of the construction
A <PIPELINE PROTECTIVE SHIELD> is a <PROTECTIVE SHIELD> that is a structure used to protect a pipeline from external damage or interference.
