description: A <QUALITY CONTROL PROCEDURE REQUIREMENT SPECIFICATION DEFINITION> is an <INSPECTION AND TESTING REQUIREMENT SPECIFICATION DEFINITION> stating the requirement for quality control procedure of a product or part of a product
superclasses: INSPECTION AND TESTING REQUIREMENT SPECIFICATION DEFINITION

description: A <QUALITY CONTROL PROCEDURE REQUIREMENTS SPECIFICATION> is an <INSPECTION AND TESTING REQUIREMENTS SPECIFICATION> stating the requirement for quality control procedure of a product or part of a product

A <QUALITY FACTOR (ELECTRICAL)>  is a <Property> that is for  non-radiating systems the measure of  the <EFFICIENCY> of a <REACTIVE ELECTRICAL CIRCUIT> that is the the <RATIO> of the <REACTANCE>  to the <RESISTANCE> expressed as   Q = |X|/R where  R is resistance and X is reactance. Defined in ISO 80000-6 (2008) 6-53

<QUALITY MANAGEMENT> is <MANAGING> all activities and tasks needed to maintain a desired level of excellence. This includes creating and implementing quality planning and assurance, as well as quality control and quality improvement
A <QUALITY MANUAL> is a <MANUAL> that describes the Quality Management System set out in accordance with selected ISO and Company standards

A <QUALITY PLAN> is a <PLAN> describing procedures to warrant quality. It shall be proposed by the supplier and shall be included in a bid. The customer and supplier shall during the contract negotiations agree upon the level of detailing for the quality pLan
A <QUALITY PROCEDURE> is an <InformationObject> and a <PROCEDURE> and a <DOCUMENT> that describes the steps for managing quality of the work
A <QUALITY REPORT> is a <REPORT> that provides a summary of any investigation, or review identifying quality impovement and learning opportunities

A <QUALITY SYSTEM APPROVAL AUTHORITY> is an <Organization> and an <APPROVER(role)> that is auhorized to perform quality system audits and issue conformance certificates, e.g. conformance to <ISO 9000> requirements

A <QUANTITY OF LIGHT> is a <Property> that is a the perceived energy of light that is the product of mean luminous flux by time. It is calculated as   Q= integral[0, delta t](Phi_v.dt) where Phi_v is A <LUMINOUS FLUX> occuring during A time interval with <DURATION> delta t
A <QUANTITY RANGE> is a <Property> that is a region of the values between the lower and upper limits of the quantity under consideration
A <QUANTITY(amount)> is a <Property> that is the amount or number of a material or abstract thing that may be expressed in numbers

A <QUANTIZING DISTORTION POWER> is a <Property> that is a measure of the distortion of a signal resulting from the process of quantizing an original signal when the values to be quantized are within the working range of the quantizer

A <QUANTUM NUMBER> is a <Property> that describes values of conserved quantities in the quantum system dynamics. Quantum Numbers are discrete sets of integers or half-integers, and give information about the size of the orbit, distribution of electrons, magnetic property, orbital size, shape, and orientation in space.
subclasses: NUCLEAR SPIN QUANTUM NUMBER, ORBITAL ANGULAR MOMENTUM QUANTUM NUMBER

description: A <QUARTER CIRCLE ORIFICE HOLE> is a <HOLE> where the wall surface, i.e. the boundary between the solid and the no-solid, is of a cylindrical nature and on the upstream edge have the form of a quarter circle.
A <QUARTER CIRCLE ORIFICE PLATE> is a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - ORIFICE PLATE> with an orifice that has the shape of a quarter circle
superclasses: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - ORIFICE PLATE

description: A <QUARTER TURN VALVE> is a <ROTARY VALVE> that is a rotary valve where the rotation of the operating mechanism is limited to 90 degrees
A <QUARTER-CIRCLE CONCENTRIC ORIFICE PLATE> is a <CONCENTRIC HOLE ORIFICE PLATE> of which the orifice is a quarter of the circumference of a circle

An object is a <QUASI UNIFORM B SPLINE CURVE> if and only if: it is a <B SPLINE CURVE>; the first and last knots are of multiplicity (degree + 1); the remaining knots are of multiplicity 1; each knot has the same difference from the preceding knot

An object is a <QUASI UNIFORM B SPLINE SOLID> if and only if: it is a <B SPLINE SOLID>; the first and last knots are of multiplicity (degree + 1); the remaining knots are of multiplicity 1; each knot has the same difference from the preceding knot

An object is a <QUASI UNIFORM B SPLINE SURFACE> if and only if: it is a <B SPLINE SURFACE>; the first and last knots are of multiplicity (degree + 1); the remaining knots are of multiplicity 1; each knot has the same difference from the preceding knot
A <QUAY> is a <FunctionalObject> that is a structure built parallel to the bank of a waterway for use as a landing place
A <QUENCH COLUMN> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <PROCESS COLUMN> intended to quench a fluid

A <QUENCH FLUID> is a <SEAL FLUID> that is a neutral fluid, usually water or steam, introduced on the atmospheric side of a seal to eliminate dangerous pumped liquid or vapor leaking through the seal and to retard formation of solids that may interfere with seal movement
A <QUENCH INTERNAL> is an <EQUIPMENT COMPONENT> that is a part of a <FIXED BED REACTOR> for catalytic hydroprocessing
A <QUENCH RING> is an <EQUIPMENT COMPONENT> that is a part of a <FIXED BED REACTOR> for catalytic hydroprocessing
A <QUENCH SYSTEM> is a <SYSTEM> intended to cool down a process
subclasses: GAS QUENCH SYSTEM, WATER QUENCH SYSTEM

description: A <QUENCH TRAY> is a <TRAY> intended to quench a fluid.

A <QUENCHED AND SELF-TEMPERED STEEL> is a <STEEL> that has received a heat treatment consisting of a quenching from a high temperature to a lower temperature resulting in a hardening and, hereafter, a slow cooling resulting in a tempering due to retained heat in the material

A <QUENCHED AND TEMPERED STEEL> is a <STEEL> that has received a heat treatment consisting of a quenching from a high temperature resulting in a hardening and, hereafter, a tempering to obtain the required properties
<QUENCHING> is the <Activity> of cooling rapidly by mixing fluids or by sumping material into a fluid
A <QUERY LANGUAGE> is an <ARTIFICIAL LANGUAGE> that is designed for requesting information from a database
subclasses: SPARQL, SQL

description: A <QUERY RESULT FILE> is an <COMPUTER FILE> that is a representation of the results of a query
subclasses: SPARQL QUERY RESULT FILE, SQL QUERY RESULT FILE

description: A <QUESTIONNAIRE> is a <FunctionalObject> with the purpose of <OBTAINING> <INFORMATION> for a survey or statistical study, and containing a set of questions with a choice of answers
subclasses: PRE-QUALIFICATION QUESTIONNAIRE

description: A <QUICK ACTING VALVE> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <VALVE> that is designed to act quickly
subclasses: QUICK DUMP VALVE, QUICK EXHAUST VALVE

description: A <QUICK ACTION CONTACT> is a <SWITCH CONTACT>, the relative displacement of which is always rapid regardless of the speed of the actuating part.
A <QUICK CONNECTOR> is a <PHYSICAL CONNECTOR> that is a temporary connection preferably between pipes which can connected and disconnected in a short time.
A <QUICK DUMP VALVE> is a <QUICK ACTING VALVE> used for quick bleed down of fluid from a hydraulic fluid line or hydrtaulic actuator
A <QUICK EXHAUST VALVE> is a <QUICK ACTING VALVE> that is connected to a special actuator on a second valve to enable quick exhaust
A <QUICK OPENING CAGE TRIM> is a <CAGE TRIM> that has a quick-opening characteristic.
A <QUICK RELEASE COUPLING> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <COUPLER> that provides easy and quick disconnection
subclasses: SPRING QUICK RELEASE COUPLING

description: A <QUICK-DISCONNECT CONNECTOR> is an <ELECTRICAL CONNECTOR> fitted with a coupling device which permits relatively rapid unmating
subclasses: LANYARD DISCONNECT CONNECTOR

description: A <QUILL SHAFT> is a <SHAFT> that is configuration by which bending moments and thrust of the driven equipment are compensated for by means of sliding teeth and/or a flexible coupling in between.

A <QUILL-SHAFT COUPLING> is a <FLEXIBLE COUPLING> designed to accommodate angular misalignment, parallel (or lateral) offset and torsional fluctuations by elastic deformation of a relatively long slender shaft. <NOTE Q>uill-shaft couplings cannot normally accommodate axial displacement.

A <QUOTATION> is an <InformationObject> and a <DOCUMENT> that is a formal statement of promise (submitted usually in response to a <RequestForQuotation) by potential supplier to supply the goods or services required by a buyer, at specified prices, and within a specified period. A quotation may also contain terms of sale and payment, and warranties. (source businessdictionary.com)
A <QUOTATION NUMBER> is an <IDENTIFYING STRING> that idenfies a <QUOTATION>
A <QUOTER> is an <INDIVIDUAL IN A ROLE> that has made a <QUOTATION>, in which goods and/or services are being offered for a price
<QUOTING> is the <Activity> of offering goods and/or services for a price
An <R RING GASKET> is a <RING JOINT GASKET> that has a symmetric cross section, and without holes.
subclasses: OCTAGONAL RING GASKET

description: A <RACK AND PINION ACTUATOR> is an <ARTEFACT> and an <ACTUATOR> that acts on the actuated device using a <RACK AND PINION GEAR>

A <RACK AND PINION GEAR> is a <GEAR> is a type of linear actuator that comprises a circular gear (the pinion) engaging a linear gear (the rack), which operate to translate rotational motion into linear motion. Driving the pinion into rotation causes the rack to be driven linearly. Driving the rack linearly will cause the pinion to be driven into a rotation.
A <RACK-AND-PANEL CONNECTOR> is an <ELECTRICAL CONNECTOR> that is one of two mating fixed connectors intended to provide a connection between a unit and its mounting rack
A <RACK-MOUNTED MEASURING INSTRUMENT> is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and a <MEASURING INSTRUMENT> that is or will be mounted in a rack

A <RADAR> is a <RADIO WAVE TRANSMITTER> for detecting the presence of objects at a distance, or ascertaining their position or motion, by transmitting short radio waves and detecting or measuring their return after being reflected

A <RADAR SCANNER> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <SCANNING DEVICE> that is a capable of detecting the presence of objects at a distance, or ascertain their position or motion, by transmitting short radio waves and detecting or measuring their return after being reflected
A <RADIAL BALL BEARING> is a <RADIAL BEARING> that is also a ball bearing.
A <RADIAL BEARING> is an<ARTEFACT> and a <BEARING> intended to support a shaft or rotor in radial direction
subclasses: ACTIVE MAGNETIC RADIAL BEARING, FIXED MULTILOBE RADIAL BEARING, HYDRODYNAMIC RADIAL BEARING, NON-DRIVEN END RADIAL BEARING, PILLOW BLOCK BEARING, RADIAL BALL BEARING, RADIAL BEARING DRIVEN END, RADIAL PLAIN BEARING, RADIAL ROLLER BEARING, RADIAL/THRUST BEARING, STEADY BEARING

description: A <RADIAL BEARING ASSEMBLY> is an <ASSEMBLY> of a <RADIAL BEARING> and associated parts
A <RADIAL BEARING BRACKET> is a <BEARING BRACKET> that is a support for a radial bearing assembly.
A <RADIAL BEARING DRIVEN END> is a <RADIAL BEARING> that is located at the driven end of a shaft.
A <RADIAL BEARING HOUSING> is a <BEARING HOUSING> intended to house a radial bearing.
A <RADIAL BEARING PAD> is a <BEARING PAD> that is intended for a radial bearing.
A <RADIAL BEARING PAD BABBIT MATERIAL> is a <BABBIT METAL> that is used for pads on radial bearings
A <RADIAL BEARING SLEEVE> is a <BEARING SLEEVE> that is a load carrying part of a radial sleeve bearing
A <RADIAL CLEARANCE> is a <CLEARANCE> in a <BEARING> between a ball and raceway perpendicular to the bearing axis.
A <RADIAL DISPLACEMENT> is a <DISTANCE> along which a <PhysicalObject> changes position in a radial direction.
subclasses: CRANK THROW

description: A <RADIAL DISPLACEMENT MEASURING INSTRUMENT> is a <MEASURING INSTRUMENT> for the measurement of <RADIAL DISPLACEMENT>, that handles the measurement result from a <RADIAL DISPLACEMENT MEASURING ELEMENT>
An <RADIAL DISPLACEMENT PROBE> is a <PROBE> for measurement of <RADIAL DISPLACEMENT>
A <RADIAL DISTANCE> is a <DISTANCE> of a thing from the axis from which it is to be measured
A <RADIAL FAN> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <FAN> with axial inlet and radial outlet
subclasses: EXPLOSION PROOF CENTRIFUGAL FAN

description: A <RADIAL FLOW GAS TURBINE> is a <GAS TURBINE> where the gas flow is made to discharge radially to the periphery of the runner
A <RADIAL FLOW MIXER IMPELLER> is a <MIXER IMPELLER> intended to produce flow along the impeller radius in distinct patterns with relatively more shear and smaller flow rates in mixing fluids.
subclasses: ANCHOR TYPE IMPELLER, BAR TURBINE IMPELLER, FLAT BLADE IMPELLER, PADDLE TYPE IMPELLER, SPIRAL BACKSWEPT TURBINE IMPELLER

description: A <RADIAL FLOW PUMP> is a <CENTRIFUGAL PUMP> that uses a radial flow impeller.
subclasses: CIRCULAR CASING PUMP, VOLUTE PUMP

description: A <RADIAL FLOW PUMP IMPELLER> is a <PUMP IMPELLER> where the flow direction is radial to the shaft axis and the values of specific speed are relatively low. It can have either a single or double suction and be of the open, closed or semi-open design.
A <RADIAL LABYRINTH SHAFT SEAL> is a <LABYRINTH SHAFT SEAL> where the labyrinth chambers are located radially around the shaft.
A <RADIAL LOAD> is a <FORCE> applied radially to the axis of an object
A <RADIAL NOZZLE> is a <NOZZLE> mounted with its axis in the direction of the centre of a shell
<RADIAL OPERATION> is <OPERATING> where each point of a given part of a network is fed along one path only

uniqueName: RADIAL OPERATION (OF A PART OF A NETWORK)
description: <RADIAL OPERATION (OF A PART OF A NETWORK)> is <OPERATING> method where each point of a given part of a network is fed along one path only
A <RADIAL PENETRATION ASSEMBLY> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <PENETRATOR> for passing lines or cables through a wall

A <RADIAL PISTON PUMP> is a <PISTON PUMP> that contains pistons arranged like wheel spokes around a cylindrical block. A drive shaft rotates this cylindrical block which pushes or slings the pistons, causing compression and expansion. The eccentricity between the piston housing and cylinder block centerlines determines the piston stroke. These pumps have a low noise level, very high loads at the lowest speeds, and high efficiency.
A <RADIAL PLAIN BEARING> is a <PLAIN BEARING> and a <RADIAL BEARING>
A <RADIAL ROLLER BEARING> is a <RADIAL BEARING> and a <ROLLER BEARING> that is capable of providing both axial and radial support simultanously.
A <RADIAL SPLIT CASING> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <CASING> where the split surface is perpendicular to the axis
subclasses: CAST RADIAL SPLIT CASING

description: A <RADIAL SPLIT MECHANICAL SEAL> is a <MECHANICAL SEAL> where the wearing parts or the hole seal can be split to make it possible to change parts without dismounting the hole machine.
subclasses: FULL SPLIT MECHANICAL SEAL, SEMI SPLIT MECHANICAL SEAL

description: A <RADIAL TURBINE MIXER> is a <DYNAMIC MIXER> where the flow moves away from to the impeller shaft
A <RADIAL/THRUST BALL BEARING> is a <BALL BEARING> and a <RADIAL/THRUST BEARING>
subclasses: Y-BEARING UNIT

description: A <RADIAL/THRUST BEARING> is a <RADIAL BEARING> and a <THRUST BEARING> that is capable of providing both axial and radial support simultanously.
subclasses: DRIVE END RADIAL/THRUST BEARING, NON-DRIVE END RADIAL/THRUST BEARING, RADIAL/THRUST BALL BEARING, RADIAL/THRUST PLAIN BEARING, RADIAL/THRUST ROLLER BEARING

description: A <RADIAL/THRUST PLAIN BEARING> is a <PLAIN BEARING> and a <RADIAL/THRUST BEARING>
A <RADIAL/THRUST ROLLER BEARING> is a <ROLLER BEARING> and a <RADIAL/THRUST BEARING>
A <RADIAN> is a <PropertyQuantification> between a <PLANE ANGLE> and a <NUMBER SPACE OF -INF TO +INF>
A <RADIAN PER SECOND> is a <PropertyQuantification> between an <ANGULAR VELOCITY> and a <NUMBER SPACE OF -INF TO +INF>
A <RADIAN PER SECOND SQUARED> is a <PropertyQuantification> between an <ANGULAR ACCELERATION> and a <NUMBER SPACE OF -INF TO +INF>

A <RADIANCE> is a <RADIANT FLUX> that is emitted, reflected, transmitted or received by a given surface, per unit solid angle per unit projected area. It is calculated as L = (dI/dA) .(1/cos(alpha)) where dI is the radiant intensity emitted from an element of a <SURFACE> with <AREA> dA and <ANGLE> alpha is an <ANGLE> between the normal to a <SURFACE> and the given direction

The <RADIANCE EXPOSURE LIGHT> is a <Property> that is a measure of the expposure of an object to light over a given <DURATION> DEFINED as   H = integral[0, delta t](E.dt) where E is the iiradiance acting during the <TIME> interval with <DURATION> delta t. Defined in ISO 80000-7 (2008) 7-20

A <RADIANCE FACTOR>  is a <Property> that is  <RATIO>  of the radiance of the <SURFACE ELEMENT>  in the given <DIRECTION>  to that of the perfect <REFLECTING> of <TRANSMITTING> reflecting or transmitting  diffuser identically irradiated and viewed. Defined in ISO 80000-7 (2008) 7-24.1
A <RADIANT ENERGY> is an <ENERGY> that is emitted, transferred or received as <RADIATION>. Defined in ISO 80000-7 (2008) 7-6
A <RADIANT ENERGY DENSITY> is a <Property> dV of that domain. Defined in ISO 80000-7 (2008) 7-7

The <RADIANT ENERGY FLUENCE> is a <Property> that is  is the amount of radiation <ENERGY> delivered per unit area over a given <DURATION> defined as  H_0 = integral[0, delta t](E_0 . dt) where E_0 is the <ENERGY> acting during  a <TIME> interval with <DURATION> delta.t. Defined in ISO 80000-7 (2008) 7-17

The <RADIANT EXITANCE> is an <Property> that is the is the <RADIANT FLUX> emitted by a <SURFACE> per <UNIT AREA> defined as at a point of a <SURFACE>, M = dPhi/ dA, where dPhi is the radiant flux leaving the element of the <SURFACE> with <AREA> dA. Defined in ISO 80000-7 (2008) 7-18
A <RADIANT FLUX> is a <Property> that is the radiant energy emitted, reflected, transmitted or received, per unit time
subclasses: RADIANCE

description: A <RADIANT INTENSITY> is a <Property> that is a measure of <RADIANT FLUX> being emitted, reflected, transmitted or received, per unit solid angle; it is calculated as I = dPhi/dOmega where dPhi is the <RADIANT FLUX> leaving the source in elementary cone containing the given direction with the solid dOmega. Defined in ISO 80000-7 (2008) 7-14
A <RADIANT POWER> is a <POWER> that is the <RADIANT ENERGY> emitted, reflected, transmitted or received, per unit <TIME>. Defined in ISO 80000-7 (2008) 7-13
<RADIATING> is the <Activity> of acting by sending out in or as if in rays
<RADIATION> is the <Activity> of <EMITTING> or <TRANSMITTING> of energy in the form of waves or particles through space or through a material medium

A <RADIATION ACTIVITY> is an <Activity> that entails a variation dN of spontaneous number of nuclei N in a particular energy state, in a sample of a radionucide, due to spontaneous nuclear transitions from this state during an infinitesimal time interval, divided by its <DURATION> dt, thus: A = -dN/dt

A <RADIATION EXPOSURE> is a <Property> that is a measure of the ionization of air due to ionizing radiation from photons, so gamma rays and X-rays. It is defined as the electric charge freed by such radiation in a specified volume of air divided by the mass of that air.
A <RADIATION MEASURING ELEMENT> is a <MEASURING ELEMENT> for detecting the level of nuclear <RADIATION>
subclasses: GAMMA DETECTING MEASURING ELEMENT

description: A <RADIATION MEASURING INSTRUMENT> is a <MEASURING INSTRUMENT> for detecting the level of nuclear <RADIATION>, that handles the measurement result from a <RADIATION MEASURING ELEMENT>
subclasses: RADIATION TRANSMITTER

description: A <RADIATION RESISTANT CABLE> is an <ELECTRICAL CABLE> in which the insulation is resistant to degradation by ionising radiation
A <RADIATION THERMOMETER> is a <HANDHELD TEMPERATURE METER> and a <TEMPERATURE GAUGE> and a <TEMPERATURE MEASURING INSTRUMENT - INFRARED>
superclasses: HANDHELD TEMPERATURE METER, TEMPERATURE GAUGE, TEMPERATURE MEASURING INSTRUMENT - INFRARED

description: A <RADIATION TRANSMITTER>is a <PROCESS VARIABLE TRANSMITTER> and a <RADIATION MEASURING INSTRUMENT>
superclasses: PROCESS VARIABLE TRANSMITTER, RADIATION MEASURING INSTRUMENT

description: A <RADIATIVE HEAT TRANSFER>  is a <HEAT TRANSFER> due to emission of electromagnetic waves
A <RADIO> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <COMMUNICATIONS DEVICE> for the transmission and/or reception of electromagnetic waves of radio frequency, especially those carrying sound messages
subclasses: RADIO RECEIVER, RADIOTELEPHONE

description: A <RADIO BEACON> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <BEACON> that  that emits identifiable radio signals intended for radio direction finding
subclasses: EMERGENCY POSITION INDICATING RADIO BEACON, NON-DIRECTIONAL BEACON

description: A <RADIO COMMUNICATION SYSTEM> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <COMMUNICATION SYSTEM> consisting of wireless operated functional units
subclasses: FIXED RADIO SYSTEM, VEHICLE-MOUNTED RADIO COMMUNICATION SYSTEM

description: A <RADIO COMPASS> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <COMPASS> that use signals from radio beacons for determining a bearing
A <RADIO PAGER> is a <RADIO RECEIVER> that is a pocket receiver for radio display paging or tone paging.
A <RADIO RECEIVER> is a <RADIO> that converts radio waves into sound or other intelligible signals
subclasses: DIGITAL RADIO, RADIO PAGER

description: A <RADIO SET> is a  <RADIO TRANSCEIVER> inteded to submit and receive radio signals
A <RADIO TRANSCEIVER> is a <TELECOMMUNICATIONS TRANSMITTER> and a <TRANSCEIVER> which has the methods of signalling through space, without connecting wires
subclasses: FIXED RADIO UNIT, RADIO SET, UHF TRANSCEIVER, VHF TRANSCEIVER

description: A <RADIO TRANSMISSION COMPONENT> is a <COMPONENT> that is a part of a <RADIO TRANSMISSION SYSTEM>
subclasses: ANTENNA TUNING UNIT

description: A <RADIO TRANSMITTER> is a <RADIO WAVE TRANSMITTER> and a <TELECOMMUNICATIONS TRANSMITTER> that propagates electromagnetic signal for radio
A <RADIO WAVE TRANSMITTER> is a <TELECOMMUNICATIONS TRANSMITTER> that emits radio waves
subclasses: RADAR, RADIO TRANSMITTER

description: <RADIOACTIVE> is an <INDIVIDUAL WITH A STATUS>  in a state of containing unstable atomic nuclei and emitting ionizing radiation or particles
subclasses: RADIOACTIVE MATERIAL

description: A <RADIOACTIVE CHEMICAL ELEMENT> is a <CHEMICAL ELEMENT> is a <RADIOACTIVE ELEMENT>
subclasses: ACTINIUM, ASTATINE

description: A <RADIOACTIVE ELEMENT> is an <Atom> that is subject to spontaneous degeneration of its nucleus accompanied by the emission of alpha particles, beta particles, or gamma rays
subclasses: RADIOACTIVE CHEMICAL ELEMENT, RADIOACTIVE METALLIC CHEMICAL ELEMENT, RADIOACTIVE TRANSURANIC CHEMICAL ELEMENT

description: <RADIOACTIVE MATERIAL> is a <Compound> with a <Status> <RADIOACTIVE>
A <RADIOACTIVE METALLIC CHEMICAL ELEMENT> is a <CHEMICAL ELEMENT> and a <METALLIC ELEMENT> and a <RADIOACTIVE ELEMENT>
superclasses: CHEMICAL ELEMENT, METALLIC ELEMENT, RADIOACTIVE ELEMENT
subclasses: CALIFORNIUM

description: A <RADIOACTIVE SOURCE> is an <ARTEFACT> and an <EMITTER> that is a known quantity of a radionuclide which emits ionizing radiation; typically one or more of the radiation types gamma rays, alpha particles, beta particles, and neutron radiation
A <RADIOACTIVE SWITCH> is a <PILOT SWITCH> that uses absorption of gamma radiation from a radioactive isotope to monitor e.g. an area.
A <RADIOACTIVE TRANSURANIC CHEMICAL ELEMENT> is a <CHEMICAL ELEMENT> and a <TRANSURANIC ELEMENT> and a <RADIOACTIVE ELEMENT>
superclasses: CHEMICAL ELEMENT, RADIOACTIVE ELEMENT, TRANSURANIC ELEMENT
subclasses: AMERICIUM, BERKELIUM, CURIUM, PLUTONIUM

description: A <RADIOACTIVITY> is a <Property> of radioactive elements in that these undergo decay emitting radiations

A <RADIOGRAPHIC INSPECTION> is <INSPECTING> using a nondestructive method that reveals the presence and nature of discontinuities in the interior of welds. This test makes use of the ability of short wavelength radiations, such as X-rays or gamma rays, to penetrate material that is opaque to ordinary light

uniqueName: RADIOGRAPHIC INSPECTION OF BUTT WELDS REQUIREMENT SPECIFICATION DEFINITION
description: A <RADIOGRAPHIC INSPECTION OF BUTT WELDS REQUIREMENT SPECIFICATION DEFINITION> is an <INSPECTION AND TESTING REQUIREMENT SPECIFICATION DEFINITION> stating the requirements of the butt welds on a product
superclasses: INSPECTION AND TESTING REQUIREMENT SPECIFICATION DEFINITION

uniqueName: RADIOGRAPHIC INSPECTION OF BUTT WELDS REQUIREMENTS SPECIFICATION
description: A <RADIOGRAPHIC INSPECTION OF BUTT WELDS REQUIREMENTS SPECIFICATION> is a <RADIOGRAPHIC INSPECTION REQUIREMENTS SPECIFICATION> of the butt welds on a product

A <RADIOGRAPHIC INSPECTION REQUIREMENT SPECIFICATION DEFINITION> is an <INSPECTION AND TESTING REQUIREMENT SPECIFICATION DEFINITION> stating the requirement for radiograpic inspection of a product or part of a product
superclasses: INSPECTION AND TESTING REQUIREMENT SPECIFICATION DEFINITION

description: A <RADIOGRAPHIC INSPECTION REQUIREMENTS SPECIFICATION> is an <INSPECTION AND TESTING REQUIREMENTS SPECIFICATION> stating the requirement for radiographic inspection of a product or part of a product
subclasses: RADIOGRAPHIC INSPECTION OF BUTT WELDS REQUIREMENTS SPECIFICATION

description: A <RADIOGRAPHIC TESTED WELD> is a <WELDED JOINT> and been radiographic tested

<RADIOGRAPHIC TESTING> is <NON-DESTRUCTIVE TESTING> of materials for hidden flaws by using the ability of short wavelength electromagnetic radiation (high energy photons) to penetrate various materials
subclasses: 10% RADIOGRAPHIC TESTING, 5% RADIOGRAPHIC TESTING

description: <RADIOGRAPHY> is <NON-DESTRUCTIVE TESTING> by means of making radiographs
A <RADIOTELEPHONE> is a <TELEPHONE> and a <RADIO> that has a transmitting and receiving unit for transmitting signals; wireless telephone
subclasses: VHF RADIOTELEPHONE

description: A <RADIUM> is an <Atom> and a <CHEMICAL ELEMENT> with symbol Ra and atomic number 88. It belongs to the alkaline earth metals
<RADIUM 226 COMPOUND> is a <Compound> mainly consisting of Radium 226, the most stable isotope of the radioactive alcaline earth metal Radium
<RADIUM 228 COMPOUND> is a <Compound> mainly consisting of Radium 228, an isotope of the radioactive alcaline earth metal Radium
A <RADIUS> is a <ShapeDimension> that is the separation between a circular arc and its centre
subclasses: BEND POINT RADIUS, BOHR RADIUS, ELECTRON RADIUS, INNER FILLET RADIUS, INSIDE FLANGE CORNER RADIUS, INSIDE WEB CORNER RADIUS, NUCLEAR RADIUS, OUTSIDE FILLET RADIUS, OUTSIDE FLANGE CORNER RADIUS, OUTSIDE WEB CORNER RADIUS, PROFILE BULB RADIUS, PROFILE FLANGE-WEB RADIUS, PROFILE INSIDE CORNER RADIUS, RADIUS OF GYRATION, RING JOINT GROOVE BOTTOM RADIUS

<RDF> is a <MODEL> that is a framework for representing information in the Web. It has an abstract syntax which serves to link all RDF-based languages and specifications. RDF graphs are sets of subject-predicate-object triples, where the elements may be IRIs, blank nodes, or datatyped literals
A <RDF DATASET> is a <STATEMENT> that consists of one <DEFAULT GRAPH> and one or more <NAMED GRAPHS>
An <RDF GRAPH> is a <STATEMENT> that is a set of <RDF TRIPLE>s
<RDF SCHEMA> is a <MODEL> that provides a data-modelling vocabulary for RDF data. RDF Schema is an extension of the basic RDF vocabulary.

An <RDF STATEMENT> is an <STATEMENT> made by a token of an RDF triple. The subject of an RDF statement is the instance of rdfs:Resource identified by the subject of the triple. The predicate of an RDF statement is the instance of rdf:Resource identified by the predicate of the triple. The object of an RDF statement is the instance of rdfs:Resource identified by the object of the triple. rdf:Statement is in the domain of the properties rdf:predicate, rdf:subject and rdf:object. Different individual rdf:Statement instances may have the same values for their rdf:predicate, rdf:subject and rdf:object properties. RDF statements are not triples in an RDF graph so their values for rdf:predicate do not need to be instances of rdf:Property in that graph, although in most cases they will be. (source: RDF 1.2 Schema)

A <RDF TRIPLE> is a <STATEMENT> that is a 3-tuple that is defined recursively as follows: If s is an IRI or a blank node, p is an IRI, and o is an IRI, a blank node, or a literal, then (s, p, o) is an RDF triple.
<RDF/XML> is  <XML> that defines the XML syntax for RDF graphs

A <REACTANCE> is a <Property> that is a measure for the opposition of a circuit element to a change in current or voltage, due to that element's inductance or capacitance. It can be calculated as  X = lm Z_ where Z_ <IMPEDANCE> and lm denotes the imaginary part
