A <SOUND ENERGY DENSITY> is a <Property> that is a time-averaged <SOUND ENERGY> in a given <VOLUME> divided by that volume

A <SOUND EXPOSURE> E is a <Property> that is the integral, over time, of squared sound pressure and a measure of the exposures to sound in given time t and is calculated using the expression E = integral[t_1, t_2](p^2.dt) where t_1 and t_2 are the starting and ending times for the integral and p is <SOUND PRESSURE>

A <SOUND EXPOSURE LEVEL> is a <Property> that is a logarithmic measure of the sound exposure of a sound relative to a reference value.  L_E = 10 lg (E/E_0)dB where E is <SOUND EXPOSURE> and the reference value is E_0 = 400muPa^2.s
A <SOUND INSULATION> is an <INSULATION> that has the capabiity of <RESISTING> <SOUND ENERGY> from being transferred

A <SOUND INTENSITY> is a <Property> that is a measure of the amount of energy flowing per unit time through a unit area that is perpendicular to the direction in which the sound waves are travelling. It is calculated as:  i = p.v where p is <SOUND PRESSURE> and v is sound particle <VELOCITY>
A <SOUND LEVEL METER> is a <MEASURING INSTRUMENT> for the measurement of sound level with a standard frequency weighting and a standard exponential time weighting

<SOUND LEVEL TEST> is <TESTING> sound levels that shall be performed as agreed between the purchaser and the vendor. <ISO> standards 3740>, 3744> and 3746> may be consulted for guidance. The soundpressure is expressed in decibele (dB) relative to a reference pressure. Decibele is defined as;
A <SOUND PARTICLE ACCELERATION> is an <ACCELERATION> of a sound particle, mostly an air molecule. It is calculated as: a = (delta v)/(delta t) where v is sound particle <VELOCITY> and t is time
A <SOUND PARTICLE DISPLACEMENT> is annstantaneous <DISPLACEMENT> of a particle in a medium from what would be its position in the absence of sound waves

A <SOUND PARTICLE VELOCITY> is a <VELOCITY> of a particle (real or imagined) in a medium as it transmits a wave. In many cases this is a longitudinal wave of pressure as with sound, but it can also be a transverse wave as with the vibration of a taut string. It is calculated as: v = (delta zeta) / (delta t) where zeta is sound particle displacement and t is time
A <SOUND POWER> is a <POWER> that is the rate at which <SOUND ENERGY> is emitted, reflected, transmitted or received per unit time

A <SOUND POWER LEVEL> is a <RATE> that is a logarithmic measure of the power of a sound relative to a reference value. It is calculated as: L_w = 10.lg (P/P_0) dB where P is <SOUND POWER> and the reference value is P_0 = 1pW
subclasses: SOUND POWER LEVEL AT MAXIMUM LOAD, SOUND POWER LEVEL AT NOMINAL LOAD, SOUND POWER LEVEL AT STANDBY

A <SPECIFIC GRAVITY AT STP> is a <SPECIFIC GRAVITY> of a liquid at a <STANDARD TEMPERATURE>  and a <STANDARD PRESSURE>
A <SPECIFIC GRAVITY MEASURING INSTRUMENT> is a <PROCESS ANALYSER> for the measurement of <SPECIFIC GRAVITY>
subclasses: AREOMETER

description: A <SPECIFIC HEAT CAPACITY> is a <Property> that is the amount of <HEAT> required to raise the <TEMPERATURE> of a substance per unit of <MASS>

uniqueName: SPECIFIC HEAT CAPACITY AT CONSTANT PRESSURE
description: A <SPECIFIC HEAT CAPACITY AT CONSTANT PRESSURE> is a <SPECIFIC HEAT CAPACITY> at a given constant <GAUGE PRESSURE>

uniqueName: SPECIFIC HEAT CAPACITY AT CONSTANT VOLUME
description: A <SPECIFIC HEAT CAPACITY AT CONSTANT VOLUME> is a <SPECIFIC HEAT CAPACITY> at a given constant <VOLUME>
A <SPECIFIC HEAT CAPACITY AT SATURATION> is a <SPECIFIC HEAT CAPACITY> at a state of <SATURATION>

uniqueName: SPECIFIC HEAT CAPACITY AT T AND P
description: A <SPECIFIC HEAT CAPACITY AT T AND P> is a <SPECIFIC HEAT CAPACITY>  at a given <TEMPERATURE> and <PRESSURE>

A <SPECIFIC HEAT CAPACITY MASS> is a <Property> that is the rate of change of thermal energy with <TEMPERATURE> per unit mass. Heat absorbed by a material divided by the increase in <TEMPERATURE> and the mass of the material (c)

A <SPECIFIC HEAT CAPACITY MOLE> is a <Property> that is the rate of change of thermal energy with <TEMPERATURE> per unit mole. Heat absorbed by a material divided by the increase in <TEMPERATURE> and the <MASS> of the material (Cm)
A <SPECIFIC HEAT RATIO> is a <RATIO> of the specific heat of a gas at a constant pressure to its specific heat at a constant volume
A <SPECIFIC HELMHOLTZ FREE ENERGY> is a <Property> that is a <HELMHOLTZ FREE ENERGY> per unit <MASS>. It is calculated as:  a = A / m where A is Helmholtz energy and m is mass
A <SPECIFIC HUMIDITY> is a <RATIO> of the mass of water vapour in a sample of moist air to the total mass of the air
A <SPECIFIC MOLAR VOLUME> is a <SPECIFIC VOLUME> at standard conditions

A <SPECIFIC OPTICAL ROTATORY POWER> is a <Property> that is a <RATIO> between the  <ANGLE> of optical rotation, and m is the  <MASS> of the optically active component as defined in ISO 80000-9 (2009) 9-59

A <SPECIFIC PRODUCTIVITY INDEX> is a <Property> that is the volumetric rate per unit <PRESSURE> change multiplied by the viscosity of the flowing fluid. This defines a fluid independent productivity index

A <SPECIFIC SPEED> is an <IndirectProperty> that refers to a <ROTATIONAL SPEED> (in rpm) that a geometrically similar impeller would need to operate in order to deliver 1 L/s of fluid at a head of 1 m (US units : 1 USgal/min at a head of 1 ft ). It is calculated as:   nq=(N*(Q^0,5))/(H^0,75) where nq=specific speed, N=rotative speed in revolutions per minute, Q=total pump flow in cubic meters per second, H=head per stage in meters
A <SPECIFIC THERMODYNAMIC ENERGY> is a <Property> that is a <THERMODYNAMIC ENERGY> per unit <MASS>. It is calculated as:  u = U / m where U is thermodynamic energy and m is mass

A <SPECIFIC VOLUME> is a <Property> defined as the number of cubic meters occupied by one kilogram of a particular <SUBSTANCE> . It is calculated as:  v=1/rho where rho is the <DENSITY> of that <SUBSTANCE>
subclasses: SPECIFIC MOLAR VOLUME

description: A <SPECIFIED-TIME RELAY> is an <ELECTRICAL RELAY> such that one or more of the times which characterize it (e.g. operate time) are subject to specified requirements, in particular concerning accuracy.
subclasses: DEPENDENT-TIME MEASURING RELAY, INDEPENDENT-TIME MEASURING RELAY

description: <SPECIFYING> is the <Activity> of defining explicitly or in detail

A <SPECTACLE BLIND> is a <LINE BLIND> and a <SPACER> and a <SPADE> that consists of two discs with equal thickness and outer diameter connected with a flat bar. One of the discs has a hole, while the other disc is without hole

A <SPECTACLES> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <TOOL> which is used to correct defects of vision or to protect the eyes that consists typically of a pair of glass or plastic lenses and the frame by which they are held in place

A <SPECTRAL ANGULAR CROSS-SECTION> is a <ShapeDimension> that is the cross section for the <EJECTION> or <SCATTERING>  in an elementsary <CONE> bisected  by the <DOLIFID ANGLE> of that cone as defined in ISO 80000-10 (2009) 10-42

uniqueName: SPECTRAL CONCENTRATION OF RADIANT ENERGY DENSITY
description: A <SPECTRAL CONCENTRATION OF RADIANT ENERGY DENSITY> is a <RATIO> of a <RADIANT ENERGY DENSITY> in an infinitesimal wavelength interval, divided by the range of interval
A <SPECTRAL CONCENTRATION OF VIBRATIONAL MODES> is a <RATIO> of a number of vibrational modes in an infinitesimal interval of angular frequency, divided by the size of that interval and by volume

A <SPECTRAL CROSS-SECTION> is a <Property> that is cross-section for a process in which the energy of the ejected or scattered particle is in an element of energy, divided by this element. sigma = integral(sigmaE.dE)

The <SPECTRAL EMISSIVITY> is a <Property>  that is a <RATIO> of how much <RADIATION> is emitted by a <SURFACE>  at a specified <WAVELENGTH> to the radiation from an <IDEAL BLACK SURFACE>> at the same <TEMPERATURE> as given by the Stefanâ€“Boltzmann law. The ratio varies from 0  to 1. Defined in ISO 80000-7 (2008) 7-21.2

The <SPECTRAL LUMINOUS EFFICACY> is a <RATIO> that is a measure of how well a Light Source produces <VISIBLE LIGHT> . It is the <RATIO> of the <MAXIMUM SPECTRAL LUMINOUS EFFICACY>  of  the light source to the <SPECTRAL LUMINOUS EFFICIENCY> . Defined in ISO 80000-7 (2008) 7-31

The <SPECTRAL LUMINOUS EFFICIENCY> is a <RATIO> that is a measure of how well a Light Source produces <LIGHT> . It is the <RATIO> of the <TOTAL RADIANT FLUX>  of  the light source to the <LIGHT> produced by it at a specified Wavelength. Defined in ISO 80000-7 (2008) 7-28

A <SPECTRAL RADIANCE FACTOR> is a <RATIO> of the spectral concentration of radiance at a point on a surface of a non-self-radiating body and in a given direction, to that of a perfect diffuser under identical irradiation conditions

uniqueName: SPECTRAL RADIANT ENERGY DENSITY IN TERMS OF WAVELENGTH
description: A <SPECTRAL RADIANT ENERGY DENSITY IN TERMS OF WAVELENGTH>  is a <Property> that is a measure of the <RADIANT ENERGY DENSITY> of <VISIBLE LIGHT> at a specified <WAVELENGTH>. Defined in ISO 80000-7 (2008) 7-8

uniqueName: SPECTRAL RADIANT ENERGY DENSITY IN TERMS OF WAVENUMBER
description: A <SPECTRAL RADIANT ENERGY DENSITY IN TERMS OF WAVENUMBER>  is a <Property> that is a measure of the <RADIANT ENERGY DENSITY> of <VISIBLE LIGHT> at a specified <WAVENUMBER>. Defined in ISO 80000-7 (2008) 7-9
A <SPECTRAL REFLECTANCE> is a <RATIO> of reflected radiant flux to incident radiant flux
A <SPECTRAL REFLECTION FACTOR> is a <RATIO> of the <SPECTRAL CONCENTRATION OF RADIANT> or <LUMINOUS FLUX> reflected to that of the incident radiation
A <SPECTRAL TRANSMISSION FACTOR> is a <RATIO> of the <SPECTRAL CONCENTRATION OF RADIANT> or <LUMINOUS FLUX> transmitted to that of the incident radiation
<SPECTROSCOPY> is the <Activity> of analysing by visual or photographic observation and the precise determination of wave lengths
subclasses: INFRARED SPECTROSCOPY

subclasses: CONDUCTION SPEED, HEAVE SPEED, LOWERING SPEED, NEUTRON SPEED, RAISING SPEED, ROTATIONAL SPEED, VELOCITY, WIND SPEED, WIND SPEED RELATIVE TO SHIP

subclasses: SPEED AT FIRST NATURAL FREQUENCY DAMPED, SPEED AT FIRST NATURAL FREQUENCY UNDAMPED

uniqueName: SPEED AT FIRST NATURAL FREQUENCY DAMPED
description: A <SPEED AT FIRST NATURAL FREQUENCY DAMPED> is a <SPEED AT FIRST NATURAL FREQUENCY> for damped condition

uniqueName: SPEED AT FIRST NATURAL FREQUENCY UNDAMPED
description: A <SPEED AT FIRST NATURAL FREQUENCY UNDAMPED> is a <SPEED AT FIRST NATURAL FREQUENCY> for undamped condition

A <SPEED MONITOR> is a <MONITOR> with the capability of receiveing signals and displaying information about speed
A <SPEED REDUCER> is  a <REDUCER> of the <SPEED> of a <PhysicalObject>
A <SPEED/TORQUE CURVE NUMBER> is an <IDENTIFYING STRING> that idenfies a speed/torque curve number
A <SPEEDER ROD> is an <INSTRUMENT COMPONENT> that connects a governor and a speed changer/control valve mechanism
A <SPEEDER SPRING> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <SPRING> intended to serve as setpoint reference for the governor travel based on spring force as function of spring compression
A <SPHERE(shape)> is a <Shape> that is defined as the set of all points equidistant from a single point in space
subclasses: BALL, SPHERICAL TANK

description: A <SPHERICAL DISC> is a <BALL TYPE GLOBE VALVE DISC> that has a spherical seating surface

A <SPHERICAL ILLUMINANCE> is a <Property> that is, at a <POINT IN SPACE>,  the amount of <LUMINOUS FLUX>  incident on a small <SPHERE>  by the cross section area of that <SPHERE>  as defined in ISO 80000-7 (2008) 7-38

A <SPHERICAL IRRADIANCE> is a <Property> that is, at a <POINT IN SPACE>, the total amount of <RADIANT FLUX>  incident on a small <SPHERE>  divided the area of the diametrical  cross section of that <SPHERE>  as defined in ISO 80000-7 (2008) 7-16

An <SPHERICAL PLAIN BEARING> is a <SLIDING TYPE BEARING> consisting of a cylindrical outer ring with a spherical supported inner ring. The bearing is suitable for alignment movements or oscillating, tilting and slewing movements.

An <SPHERICAL ROLLER BEARING> is a <ROLLER BEARING> provided with two rows of rollers with a common sphered raceway in the outer ring. The two inner ring raceways are inclined at an angle to the bearing axis. This bearing is of the self-aligning type and can also accommodate for limited axial loads in both directions.

An <SPHERICAL ROLLER THRUST BEARING> is a <ROLLER BEARING> utilizing spherical rollers between an outer and inner ring where the raceways are positioned at an angle to the bearing axis. These types of bearings can handle both axial and radial loads as well as misalignment to the shaft axis.
A <SPHERICAL SURFACE> is an <ELEMENTARY SURFACE> and an <ELLIPSOIDAL SURFACE>; there is a centre point that is equi-distance from each point in the surface
subclasses: CANONICALLY PARAMETERISED SPHERICAL SURFACE

description: A <SPHERICAL TANK> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <TANK> which has a <SPHERE(shape)> shape
An <SPHERICAL VESSEL> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <VESSEL> with the shape of a <SPHERE(shape)>
A <SPIDER> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <DISTRIBUTOR> intended to evenly distribute a fluid and that has a typical spider shape
subclasses: REFLUX SPIDER

description: An <SPIGOT FACE FLANGE END> is a <FLANGED PIPE END> that has a spigot gasket contact face
An <SPIGOT FLANGE> is a <PIPE FLANGE> where the flanged end is a spigot face flanged end.
subclasses: SOCKET WELDING SPIGOT FLANGE, WELD NECK SPIGOT FLANGE

An <SPILL OIL> is an <OIL>, normally lubrication oil, that has been used and is treated as waste
<SPILLING> is the <Activity> of acting by causing or allowing to splash, pour, or fall out and be wasted, lost or scattered
A <SPIN> is a <Property> that is a measure of the internal <ANGULAR MOMENTUM> of a <PARTICLE> or a particle system. Defined in ISO 80000-10 (2009) 10-11
A <SPINDLE> is a <SHAFT> acting as a revolving axis or as a pin on which another element revolves.
subclasses: UNLOADER INDICATOR SPINDLE

description: A <SPIRAL BACKSWEPT TURBINE IMPELLER> is a <RADIAL FLOW MIXER IMPELLER> that is of the open type and provided with radially curved blades.
A <SPIRAL BINDER TAPE> is a <CABLE LAYER> that is a metallic tape wound in an open helix on wire armour to keep it in place
A <SPIRAL HEAT EXCHANGER> is an <ARTEFACT> and  a <HEAT EXCHANGER> in which a pair of plates is formed into a spiral
types: ClassOfInanimatePhysicalObject, HEATERS, COOLERS AND HEAT TRANSFER

description: A <SPIRAL SERRATED FLANGE FACE FINISH> is a <Feature> that Is a <FACE> has a profile of a spiral groove
A <SPIRAL SOCK VALVE> is a <MEMBRANE VALVE> that controls flow of powders by means of a twisted fabric tube or sock
A <SPIRAL SPRING> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <SPRING> formed by coiling a steel ribbon into an elongated flat spiral or a helix of increasing diameter

A <SPIRAL TUBE HEAT EXCHANGER> is a <SHELL AND COIL HEAT EXCHANGER> in which a single tube is formed into a spiral, i.e. the tube formes a plane curve and winds about a fixed pole from which it continually recedes
types: ClassOfInanimatePhysicalObject, HEATERS, COOLERS AND HEAT TRANSFER

description: A <SPIRAL WOUND GASKET> is a <PIPE FLANGE GASKET> that is made of spirally wound metal windings and filler materials.
A <SPIRAL-BEVEL GEAR> is a <GEAR> that has spiral-bevel teeth.
A <SPIRAL-BEVEL GEARBOX> is a <CROSSED AXIS GEARBOX> where the input and output shafts normally are standing 90> deg. to each other utilizing a pinion and gear with spiral-bevel gear teeth.

A <SPIRAL-PIN> is an <SPRING PIN> with a spiral-shaped cross-sedtion (like a coiled plate). It deforms elastically in the radial direction when driven. The resiliency of the pin material locks the pin in place.
An <SPLASH CONE> is an <EQUIPMENT INTERNAL> and a <REDUCER> capable of reducing a stream velocity into a separator (vessel) from a pipe
<SPLASH GOGGLES> are <PROTECTIVE GLASSES> that are intended to protect the eyes especially against droplets of liquid
An <SPLINE> is a <Feature> that is a number of relatively narrow key ways formed external on a shaft or internal inside the hole of a hub. Used instead of shaft key for maximum strength
subclasses: EXTERNAL SPLINE, INTERNAL SPLINE

description: A <SPLINED BORE COUPLING HUB> is a <COUPLING HUB> that has a splined bore
An <SPLINED SHAFT> is a <SHAFT> with a number of relatively narrow keys formed integral with the shaft , somewhat resembling long gear-teeth; produced by milling longitudinal grooves in the shaft.
An <SPLIT BALL VALVE BODY> is a <BALL VALVE BODY> that can be split, thus allowing service to be performed on the closure member, valve interior, etc.
subclasses: BOLTED SPLIT BALL VALVE BODY

subclasses: BOLTED BODY BALL VALVE, THREE PIECE BALL VALVE, TWO PIECE BALL VALVE

An <SPLIT ENGINE BLOCK> is a <PISTON ENGINE BLOCK> that is split, i.e. it is made of more than one part.
An <SPLIT FLOW SHELL> is a <HEAT EXCHANGER SHELL> where flow is splitted by one split plate.

subclasses: SINGLE EXPANDING SPLIT GATE

subclasses: CAPACITOR MOTOR, REACTOR START SPLIT PHASE MOTOR, RESISTANCE START SPLIT PHASE MOTOR

subclasses: COTTER PIN

An <SPLIT SHEAR RING> is a <RING> that is a positoning/locking ring for slip-on flange
A <SPLIT THROW WINDING> is a <TWO LAYER WINDING> in which the conductors which constitute a coil side in one slot are not all together in another slot
An <SPLIT TUBING HANGER> is a <TUBING HANGER> that is made in two parts which will be clamped around the tubing string.
An <SPLIT WEDGE GATE VALVE> is a <WEDGE GATE VALVE> having a wedge comprising of two parts in order to provide flexibility and resistance to thermal wedging

A <SPLITTER> is a <DISTILLATION COLUMN> and a <SPLITTER(function)> intended to split a fluid into two fractions

<SPLITTING UP> is the <Activity> of separating by dividing in parts or portions

A <SPOTLIGHT> is a <PROJECTOR> casting a narrow and intense beam.
A <SPOUT> is an <ELECTRICAL SOCKET> that acts as a female contact for a device such as a circuit breaker to be racked into position for operation.

A <SPRAY CAN HAZARDOUS WASTE MATTER> is a <HAZARDOUS WASTE MATTER> that consists of spray cans

A <TemporalWholePart> is a <CompositionOfIndividual> that indicates that one <PossibleIndividual> is a temporal part of another <PossibleIndividual>. The spatial extent of the temporal part is that of the temporal whole for the period of the existence of the temporal part. <Relationship>s that apply to the whole <PossibleIndividual> also apply to the temporal parts of the <PossibleIndividual>, except when the relationships relate to the temporal nature of the whole. So if a <PossibleIndividual> is connected so are all its temporal parts, but being a <WholeLifeIndividual> is not inherited by its temporal parts. NOTE Since <TemporalWholePart> is transitive (inherited from its supertype) a hierarchy of temporal parts is possible, with a <WholeLifeIndividual> at the top

A <THEOREM> is a <PROPOSITION> that is proved by a chain of reasoning, or a truth established by means of accepted truths

The diffuser is conically shaped

A <THERMAL CONDUCTIVITY ANALYSER>is a <PROCESS ANALYSER> that is intended to determine a physical property that is named thermal conductivity

superclasses: GAS ANALYSER, INSTRUMENTATION ITEM, THERMAL CONDUCTIVITY ANALYSER

description: <THERMAL CONVERSION> is the <Activity> of converting by the application of heat and pressure
A <THERMAL CRACKER> is a <CRACKER that has the capability of <THERMAL CRACKING>
<THERMAL CRACKING> is <CRACKING> by the application of heat and pressure

A  <THERMAL DIFFUSION COEFFICIENT> is a  <Property> that is the proportionality coefficient in the equation which establishes the dependence of the <THERMAL DIFFUSION RATIO> to the <DIFFUSION COEFFICENT> as defined in ISO 80000-9 (2009) 9-47

A <THERMAL DIFFUSION FACTOR> is a dimensionless <IndirectProperty> that refers to a  <THERMAL DIFFUSION> that expresses the relationship between the <THERMAL DIFFUSION RATIO> and the <DIFFUSION COEFFICIENT>  as defined in ISO 80000-9 (2009) 9-46.2

A <THERMAL DIFFUSION RATIO> is a <Property> that In the steady state of a <BINARY MIXTURE> in which <THERMAL DIFFUSION> occurs describes the relationship between the <RATIO> of the two substances and the <TEMPERATURE>  as defined in ISO 80000-9 (2009) 9-46.1

A <THERMAL DIFFUSIVITY> is a <Property> that is a measure of the rate of transfer of heat of a material from the hot side to the cold side and is the thermal conductivity divided by density and specific heat capacity at constant pressure. It is calculated as:     a = lambda/( rho.cp) where lambda is the<THERMAL CONDUCTIVITY>, rho is <MASS DENSITY> and cp the mass heat capacity at constant pressure
<THERMAL DRYING> is <DRYING> by the application of heat and pressure

A <THERMAL ELECTRICAL RELAY> is a <DEPENDENT-TIME MEASURING RELAY> that is intended to protect an equipment from electrical thermal damage by the measurement of the current flowing in the protected equipment and by a characteristic curve stimulating its thermal behaviour.
A <THERMAL ELECTROMOTIVE FORCE> is an <ELECTROMOTIVE FORCE> arising from a difference in temperature at two points along a circuit
A <THERMAL ELEMENT SHEATH> is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and a <PRESSURIZED CONTAINER> that is made to act as a protective layer covering a <TEMPERATURE ELEMENT>

A <THERMAL ENERGY STREAM is a <Stream> and an <THERMAL ENERGY>

<THERMAL INSULATION> is <INSULATION> that is capable of <PROTECTING> against loss of heat

subclasses: MINERAL WOOL, REFRACTORY MATERIAL

Thermal neutrons are neutrons slowed down to be in thermal equilibrium with its surroundings. The measure unit is cross-section area pr. nucleus of the substance. (barns/atom) (1 barn = 10**-24 cm2)

A <THERMAL NEUTRON ABSORPTION CROSS-SECTION> is a <Property> that is a measure of the substances ability to absorb <THERMAL NEUTRONS> . Thermal neutrons are neutrons slowed down to be in thermal equilibrium with its surroundings. The measure unit is <CROSS-SECTION AREA> pr. nucleus of the substance. (barns/atom) (1 barn = 10**-24 cm2)

<THERMAL PROTECTION> is <PROTECTING> against unwanted temperatures

A <THERMAL RATED WINDING> is a <WINDING> in which the temperature rise is within specified limits.

A <THERMAL UTILIZATION FACTOR (NUCLEAR)> is a <RATIO> absorbed

As the thermal wheel rotates, heat is captured from the exhaust air stream in one half of the rotation and released to the fresh air stream in the other half of the rotation. Thus waste heat energy from the exhaust air stream is transferred to the matrix material and then from the matrix material to the fresh air stream

A <THERMISTOR> is a <TEMPERATURE MEASURING ELEMENT - RESISTANCE> that use a semiconductor device to change resistance that increases with increasing temperature, and is used for the sensitive measurement and control
<THERMITE WELDING> is <FUSION WELDING> that produces coalescence of metals by heating them with superheated liquid metal from a chemical reaction, with or without the application of pressure

A <THERMOCOUPLE EXTENSION CABLE> is a <SIGNAL CONVEYING ITEM> and a <ELECTRICAL CABLE> consisting of conductors of the same nature as the thermocouple elements, extending it to the reference junction and having the same thermo-electric properties as those of the thermocouple within the whole temperature range of utilisation
A <THERMOCOUPLE SIGNAL CONNECTION> is an <INSTRUMENT SIGNAL CONNECTION>  for letting pass an electrical <SIGNAL> from a <THERMOCOUPLE> to another <PROCESS INSTRUMENTATION ITEM>

A <THERMODYNAMIC TEMPERATURE> is a <Property> that is defined by the third law of thermodynamics in which the theoretically lowest temperature is the null or zero point. At this point, absolute zero, the particle constituents of matter have minimal motion and can become no colder
A <THERMOELECTRIC TRANSDUCER> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <TRANSDUCER> that by sensing variations in heat differentials is capable of producing a quantitative electric signal

subclasses: THERMO-MECHANICAL ROLLED STEEL

description: A <THERMO-MECHANICAL ROLLED STEEL> is a <THERMO-MECHANICAL CONTROLLED PROCESSED STEEL> that is rolled in such a manner that the final deformation was carried out in a certain temperature range leading to a material condition with certain properties which can not be achieved or repeated by heat treatment alone

A <TORTUOSITY> is a <Property> that is a measure of the geometric complexity of a porous medium. Tortuosity is a ratio that characterizes the convoluted pathways of fluid diffusion and electrical conduction through porous media. In the fluid mechanics of porous media, tortuosity is the ratio of the length of a streamline&amp;#226;€”a flow line or path&amp;#226;€”between two points to the straight-line distance between those points. Tortuosity is thus related to the ratio of a fluid&amp;amp;amp;#39;s diffusion coefficient when it is not confined by a porous medium to its effective diffusion coefficient when confined in a porous medium. Tortuosity is also related to the formation factor, which is the ratio of electrical resistivity of a conductive fluid in a porous medium to the electrical resistivity of the fluid itself

A <VALVE SEAT RING> is a <SUPPORT RING> that is intended to support the valve closure member. One face of the ring forms the valve seat which may contain a seat insert. The reverse face is fastened to the body of the valve by a threaded portion or by swaging in small bore valves.

description: A <VISCOSITY AT T UPPER LIMIT FLOW> is a <VISCOSITY AT T> which is the viscosity of a fluid at an <UPPER LIMIT FLOW>
A <VISCOUS SHEAR TORSIONAL VIBRATION DAMPER> is a <TORSIONAL VIBRATION DAMPER> that uses viscous fluid as damping medium
A <VISIBILITY> is a <STRAIGHT LINEAR DISTANCE> under the given weather conditions to which it is possible to see horizontaly in daylight without instrumental assistance
A <VISIBLE COLOUR> is <LIGHT> with <WAVELENGTH>s in the segment of the electromagnetic spectrum that the human eye can view, typically 380 - 700 nanometers.
subclasses: BLACK, BLUE, BROWN, GREEN, GREY, ORANGE, PINK, PURPLE, RED, VIOLET, WHITE, YELLOW

description: A <VISUAL ALARM LUMIAIRE> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <LUMINAIRE> that produces a light that reperesents an alarm
<VISUAL EXAMINATION> is the <Activity> of examining by observation
<VITON> is a <FLUOROELASTOMER> and a <RUBBER> that is a trade name (DuPont Performance Elastomers L.L.C.) for a synthetic rubber based on a copolymer of of vinylidene fluoride and hexa-fluoropropene
A <VND> is a <CURRENCY> called 'Dong' and used in VIET NAM
<VOID> is an <InformationRepresentation>, typed as <STATUS CODE>, denoting the <Status> <OBSOLETE>
<VOLCANIC ROCK> is <ROCK> formed from lava erupted from a volcano. In other words, it differs from other igneous rock by being of volcanic origin
subclasses: PERLITE

description: A <VOLT> is a <PropertyQuantification> between an <ELECTRIC POTENTIAL DIFFERENCE> or an <ELECTROMOTIVE FORCE> and a <NUMBER SPACE OF -INF TO +INF>

types: Scale, UOM (SCALE), ELECTRIC FIELD STRENGTH SCALE CLASS

description: A <VOLT PER METRE> is a <PropertyQuantification> between an <ELECTRIC FIELD STRENGTH> and a <NUMBER SPACE OF -INF TO +INF>
types: Scale, UOM (SCALE), ELECTRIC FIELD STRENGTH SCALE CLASS

description: A <VOLTAGE> is a <Property> expressed by U_ab = V_a - V_b where V_a and V_b are the electric potentials at points a and b, respectively
subclasses: BASIC IMPULSE LEVEL, IMPEDANCE VOLTAGE, IMPULSE VOLTAGE, NEGATIVE SEQUENCE VOLTAGE COMPONENT, NEUTRAL POINT DISPLACEMENT VOLTAGE, PHASE TO EARTH VOLTAGE, PHASE TO NEUTRAL VOLTAGE, PHASE TO PHASE VOLTAGE, POSITIVE SEQUENCE VOLTAGE COMPONENT, SHORT CIRCUIT REACTANCE VOLTAGE, SHORT CIRCUIT RESISTANCE VOLTAGE, SOURCE VOLTAGE, SUPPLY VOLTAGE, TOUCH VOLTAGE, TRANSFORMER IMPEDANCE VOLTAGE, ZERO SEQUENCE VOLTAGE COMPONENT

description: A <VOLTAGE CHANGE FACTOR> is a <RATIO> of a voltage after the change to the voltage prior to the change
A <VOLTAGE CONTROLLED BUS> is an <ARTEFACT> and an <ELECTRICAL NODE> function with predetermined active input power and node voltage magnitude
<VOLTAGE CONTROLLING> is <CONTROLLING> network voltages to values within a given range
subclasses: IN-PHASE VOLTAGE CONTROLLING, QUADRATURE VOLTAGE CONTROLLING

description: <VOLTAGE DECREASE> is <VOLTAGE TRANSFORMING> to decrease the level of voltage
A <VOLTAGE DEPENDENT RESISTOR> is a <NON-LINEAR VARIABLE RESISTOR> in which the resistance depends on the voltage across it.
A <VOLTAGE DETECTOR> is an <ELECTRIC VARIABLE DETECTOR> and a <VOLTAGE MEASURING INSTRUMENT> using a <VOLTAGE MEASURING ELEMENT> that is designed to detect the presence of an <ELECTRIC POTENTIAL>
superclasses: ELECTRIC VARIABLE DETECTOR, VOLTAGE MEASURING INSTRUMENT
subclasses: LINE VOLTAGE DETECTOR

description: A <VOLTAGE DIVIDER> is an <ELECTRICAL COMPONENT> that is a linear resistor or series of resistors which can be tapped at any intermediate point to obtain a voltage equal to a desired fraction of the voltage applied between its ends.
A <VOLTAGE GENERATOR> is an <ELECTRIC GENERATOR> That supplies voltage at low energy for testing
<VOLTAGE INCREASE> is <VOLTAGE TRANSFORMING> to increase the level of voltage
A <VOLTAGE LOOP> is an <ELECTRONIC CIRCUIT> that uses voltage for signaling.
A <VOLTAGE MAP> is an <InformationObject> and a <MAP> that is the consistent presentation of the voltages at the major nodes of a network under specified operating conditions
A <VOLTAGE MATCHING TRANSFORMER> is a <INSTRUMENT VOLTAGE TRANSFORMER> for matching the rated secondary voltage of the main voltage transformer to the rated voltage of the burden
A <VOLTAGE MEASURING INSTRUMENT> is an <ELECTRIC VARIABLE MEASURING INSTRUMENT> for measurement of <VOLTAGE>
subclasses: VOLTAGE DETECTOR, VOLTAGE TRANSMITTER, VOLTMETER

description: A <VOLTAGE MONITOR> is  a <MONITOR> with the capability of receiveing signals and displaying information about voltage level

A <VOLTAGE PHASOR> is a <PHASOR> for a <VOLTAGE> in a 3-phase system. It is calulted as;  u = U .cos(omegat + alpha) where u is the voltage, omega is angular frequency, t is time, and alpha is initial phase then U_ = U.e^(Jalpha)
A <VOLTAGE RATED CABLE> is an <ELECTRICAL CABLE> conforming to a specification for highest allowable voltage under rated conditions
A <VOLTAGE REGULATOR> is a <REGULATOR> designed to automatically maintain a constant voltage level
A <VOLTAGE RELAY> is an <ELECTRICAL APPARATUS> and a <RELAY> that is designed for voltage
A <VOLTAGE SCALE CLASS> is a <DOMAIN SCALE CLASS> for <VOLTAGE>
A <VOLTAGE TO CURRENT SIGNAL CONVERTER> is a <SIGNAL CONVERTER> that is capable for converting an input voltage signal into a current output signal
A <VOLTAGE TO PRESSURE SIGNAL CONVERTER> is a <SIGNAL CONVERTER> that is capable for converting a voltage input signal into proportional linear pneumatic output signal
A <VOLTAGE TO VOLTAGE SIGNAL CONVERTER> is a <SIGNAL CONVERTER> that is capable for converting a voltage input signal to a voltage output signal
A <VOLTAGE TRANSFORMER PRIMARY WINDING> is a <TRANSFORMER PRIMARY WINDING> to which the voltage to be transformed is applied
A <VOLTAGE TRANSFORMER SECONDARY WINDING> is a <TRANSFORMER SECONDARY WINDING> that supplies voltage to the circuits of measuring instruments, meters, protective or control devices
<VOLTAGE TRANSFORMING> is <ELECTRICITY TRANSFORMING> to bring the level of voltage up or down
subclasses: VOLTAGE DECREASE, VOLTAGE INCREASE

description: A <VOLTAGE TRANSMITTER> is an < ELECTRICAL VARIABLE TRANSMITTER> and a <VOLTAGE MEASURING INSTRUMENT>
superclasses: ELECTRICAL VARIABLE TRANSMITTER, VOLTAGE MEASURING INSTRUMENT

description: A <VOLTAGE-REFERENCE DIODE> is a <SEMICONDUCTOR DIODE> that develops across its terminals a reference voltage of specified accuracy, when biased to operate within a specified current range.
A <VOLTAGE-REGULATOR DIODE> is a <SEMICONDUCTOR DIODE> that develops across its terminals an essentially constant voltage throughout specified current range.
A <VOLT-AMPERE METER> is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and a <POWER MEASURING INSTRUMENT> intended to measure apparent power (volt-ampere)
subclasses: INTEGRATING VOLT-AMPERE METER

description: A <VOLT-AMPERE-HOUR METER> is an <ELECTRICAL ENERGY MEASURING INSTRUMENT> and an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> intended to measure apparent energy by integrating apparent power with respect to time
superclasses: ELECTRICAL ENERGY MEASURING INSTRUMENT, INSTRUMENTATION ITEM

description: A <VOLTMETER> is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and a <VOLTAGE MEASURING INSTRUMENT> for measuring the pressure of electricity in volts
subclasses: DYNAMOMETER VOLTMETER, ELECTROSCOPE, ELECTROSTATIC INSTRUMENT, INTEGRATING VOLT METER, PEAK VOLTMETER, SPARK GAP METER

description: A <VOLUME> is a <Property> that is a measure of three-dimensional space enclosed by a closed surface, including the space that a substance (solid, liquid, gas, or plasma) or a shape occupies or contains
subclasses: BULK VOLUME, CRITICAL VOLUME, DISPLACEMENT PER REVOLUTION, FIRE EXTINGUISER PROPELLANT GAS CAPACITY, FIRE EXTINGUISING AGENT CAPACITY, GAS LIFT VOLUME, INTERNAL VOLUME, PRE-CHARGE VOLUME, SHIPPING VOLUME, VOLUME PER STROKE

description: A <VOLUME CONCENTRATION> is a <PERCENTAGE> that is a measure of the concentration of a substance in a solution.
A <VOLUME CONTROL DAMPER> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <GAS FLOW DAMPER> that has the capability of <DAMPING> a <GAS> flow whilst controlling the volume <GAS> flow in a duct system
A <VOLUME FLOW INDICATOR> is a <FLOW INDICATOR> that measures the flow as a volume per time
A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT> is a <FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT> that is used to measure <VOLUME FLOW RATE>
subclasses: ORIFICE PLATE FLOWMETER ASSEMBLY, VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE, VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - FORCE BALANCE, VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - LEVEL-TO-FLOW OPEN CHANNEL, VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - POSITIVE DISPLACEMENT, VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - SONIC NOZZLE, VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - VARIABLE AREA, VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - VELOCITY

uniqueName: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - ACOUSTIC DOPPLER
description: A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - ACOUSTIC DOPPLER> is a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - VELOCITY> measuring the velocity of particles in a remote sampling volume based upon the Doppler shift effect; records velocity components at a single point with a relatively high frequency
A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - ANEMOMETRIC> is a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - VELOCITY> that can be the sensing element of an ANEMOMETER or wind gauge

A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - AREA-VELOCITY> is a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - LEVEL-TO-FLOW OPEN CHANNEL> that calculates flow in an open channel by measuring the level to determine the cross section, and it measures the fluid velocity; subequently these two values are multiplied to arrive at the <VOLUME FLOW RATE>
superclasses: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - LEVEL-TO-FLOW OPEN CHANNEL
subclasses: WEIR FLOW METER

uniqueName: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - BROAD-CRESTED WEIR
description: A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - BROAD-CRESTED WEIR> is a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - WEIR> that is a flat-crested structure, with a long crest compared to the flow thickness

A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - CONE> is a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE> that works with the same basic principles as Venturi and Orifice type DP meters, but do not require the same upstream and downstream piping. The cone acts as a conditioning device as well as a differential pressure producer
superclasses: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE

description: A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - CURRENT> is a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - LEVEL-TO-FLOW OPEN CHANNEL> that where a propeller is traversed over the area of a channel and velocities averaged to calculate total flow. This may be on the order of hundreds of cubic meters per second. The flow must be kept steady during the traverse of the current meters. Methods for testing hydroelectric turbines are given in IEC standard 60041
superclasses: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - LEVEL-TO-FLOW OPEN CHANNEL

uniqueName: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - DALL TUBE
description: A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - DALL TUBE> is a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE> that is a shortened version of a Venturi meter, with a lower pressure drop than an orifice plate. As with these flow meters the flow rate in a Dall tube is determined by measuring the pressure drop caused by restriction in the conduit
superclasses: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE

uniqueName: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE
description: A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE> is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT> that measures the differential pressure across a <MEASURING ELEMENT> in order to measure <VOLUME FLOW RATE>
superclasses: INSTRUMENTATION ITEM, VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT
subclasses: VENTURI TUBE ASSEMBLY, VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - CONE, VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - DALL TUBE, VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - ELBOW, VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - ELLIPTIC THROAT, VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - FLOW NOZZLE, VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - ORIFICE PLATE, VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - PITOT TUBE, VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - SEGMENTAL WEDGE, VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - V-CONE, VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - VENTURI TUBE

description: A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - ELBOW> is a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE> where the fluid passes through a pipe elbow. The pressure at the outside radius of the elbow increases due to centrifugal force
superclasses: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE

description: A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - ELECTROMAGNETIC> is a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - VELOCITY> that uses a magnetic field applied to the metering tube, which results in a potential difference proportional to the flow velocity perpendicular to the flux lines. The potential difference is sensed by electrodes aligned perpendicular to the flow and the applied magnetic field. The physical principle at work is Faraday&amp;#39;s law of electromagnetic induction. The magnetic flow meter requires a conducting fluid and a nonconducting pipe liner

uniqueName: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - ELECTROMAGNETIC INSERTION
description: A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - ELECTROMAGNETIC INSERTION> is a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - VELOCITY> that uses electromagnetic principles to measure flow at a point inside the process

uniqueName: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - ELLIPTIC THROAT
description: A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - ELLIPTIC THROAT> is a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE> that has a tapered restriction of elliptic profile in its passage and measures flow rate by measuring differential pressure between the front part and the throat of the restriction
superclasses: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE

uniqueName: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - FLOW NOZZLE
description: A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - FLOW NOZZLE> is a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE> that utilizes a flow nozzle with a smooth guided entry and a sharp exit place in the pipe to change the flow field and create a pressure drop that is used to calculate the flow velocity
superclasses: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE

description: A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - FLUME> is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING INSTRUMENT> that handles the measurement results of a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - FLUME>
superclasses: INSTRUMENTATION ITEM, VOLUME FLOW MEASURING INSTRUMENT

uniqueName: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - FORCE BALANCE
description: A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - FORCE BALANCE> is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT>, where the measured process signal is countebalanced by the outpur signal
superclasses: INSTRUMENTATION ITEM, VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT
subclasses: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - IMPACT, VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - TARGET, VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - VANE

description: A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - GEAR> is a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - POSITIVE DISPLACEMENT> that uses gears to divide and meter the flow
superclasses: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - POSITIVE DISPLACEMENT
subclasses: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - HELICAL GEAR, VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - OVAL GEAR

uniqueName: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - HELICAL GEAR
description: A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - HELICAL GEAR> is a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - GEAR> that is a flow meter that gets its name from the shape of its gears or rotors. These rotors resemble the shape of a helix, which is a spiral-shaped structure. As the fluid flows through the meter, it enters the compartments in the rotors, causing the rotors to rotate. Flowrate is calculated from the speed of rotation

A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - HELIX> is a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - POSITIVE DISPLACEMENT> that is a type of turbine flow meter that comprises a rotor with helical blades inserted axially in the flow, much like a ducted fan
superclasses: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - POSITIVE DISPLACEMENT

description: A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - IMPACT> is a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - FORCE BALANCE> that measures the impact force of a fluid on a plate and outputs a signal representative of flow
superclasses: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - FORCE BALANCE

uniqueName: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - LASER DOPPLER
description: A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - LASER DOPPLER> is a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - VELOCITY> that uses a beam of laser light impinging on a moving particle; the light will be partially scattered with a change in wavelength proportional to the particles speed (the Doppler effect)

uniqueName: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - LEVEL-TO-FLOW OPEN CHANNEL
description: A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - LEVEL-TO-FLOW OPEN CHANNEL> is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT> where behind a <WEIR> or in a <FLUME> the level of the water is measured at a designated point in a hydraulic structure using various secondary devices (bubblers, ultrasonic, float, and differential pressure are common methods). This level is converted to a <VOLUME FLOW RATE>
superclasses: INSTRUMENTATION ITEM, VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT
subclasses: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - AREA-VELOCITY, VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - CURRENT, VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - WEIR

uniqueName: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - MULTIPLE JET
description: A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - MULTIPLE JET> is a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - VELOCITY> that is a velocity type meter that has an impeller that rotates horizontally on a vertical shaft. The impeller element is in a housing in which multiple inlet ports direct the fluid flow at the impeller causing it to rotate in a specific direction in proportion to the flow velocity. This meter works mechanically much like a single jet meter except that the ports direct the flow at the impeller equally from several points around the circumference of the element, not just one point; this minimizes uneven wear on the impeller and its shaft

uniqueName: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - NUTATING DISC
description: A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - NUTATING DISC> is a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - POSITIVE DISPLACEMENT> that uses a disk which fits closely in a measuring chamber. As the fluid enters one side of the partition and leaves through the other side, it makes the disk to wobble. The number of revolutions made by a small shaft attached to the disk will indicate the volume of flow
superclasses: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - POSITIVE DISPLACEMENT

description: A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - OPTICAL> is a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - VELOCITY> that is a flow meter that uses light to determine flow rate. Small particles which accompany natural and industrial gases pass through two laser beams focused a short distance apart in the flow path. Laser light is scattered when a particle crosses the first beam. The detecting optics collects scattered light on a photodetector, which then generates a pulse signal. As the same particle crosses the second beam, the detecting optics collect scattered light on a second photodetector, which converts the incoming light into a second electrical pulse. By measuring the time interval between these pulses, the gas velocity is calculated

uniqueName: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - ORIFICE PLATE
description: A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - ORIFICE PLATE> is a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE> that is a plate with a hole through it, placed in the flow; it constricts the flow, and measuring the pressure differential across the constriction gives the flow rate. It is basically a crude form of Venturi meter, but with higher energy losses. There are three type of orifice: concentric, eccentric, and segmental
superclasses: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE
subclasses: CONCENTRIC HOLE ORIFICE PLATE, ECCENTRIC HOLE ORIFICE PLATE, PADDLE ORIFICE PLATE, QUARTER CIRCLE ORIFICE PLATE, SEGMENTAL ORIFICE PLATE, UNIVERSAL TYPE ORIFICE PLATE

uniqueName: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - OVAL GEAR
description: A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - OVAL GEAR> is a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - GEAR> that is a positive displacement meter that uses two or more oblong gears configured to rotate at right angles to one another, forming a T shape

A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - PISTON> is a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - POSITIVE DISPLACEMENT> that is utilizing a piston closely fitted into a cylindrical chamber with a pair of slots that are progressively uncovered as the pressure differential makes the piston oscillate/spin around a control roller in the centre of the chamber
superclasses: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - POSITIVE DISPLACEMENT

uniqueName: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - PITOT TUBE
description: A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - PITOT TUBE> is a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE> that is a pressure measuring device used to measure fluid flow velocity by determining the stagnation pressure and static pressure. Bernoulli&amp;amp;amp;#39;s equation used to calculate the dynamic pressure and hence fluid velocity
superclasses: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE
subclasses: MULTIPORT PITOT TUBE

uniqueName: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - POSITIVE DISPLACEMENT
description: A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - POSITIVE DISPLACEMENT> is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT> that measures the volumetric flow rate of a liquid or gas by separating the flow stream into known volumes and counting them over time
superclasses: INSTRUMENTATION ITEM, VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT
subclasses: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - GEAR, VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - HELIX, VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - NUTATING DISC, VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - PISTON, VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - ROTARY

description: A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - ROTARY> is a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - POSITIVE DISPLACEMENT> that uses eccentrically mounted drums to divide and meter the flow
superclasses: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - POSITIVE DISPLACEMENT

uniqueName: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - ROTATING ELEMENT
description: A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - ROTATING ELEMENT> is a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - VELOCITY> that uses the rotation of a shaped element to measure flow
subclasses: TURBINE FLOW METER ROTOR

uniqueName: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - SEGMENTAL WEDGE
description: A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - SEGMENTAL WEDGE> is a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE> that measures a differentail pressure acros an interior segmental wedge
superclasses: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE

uniqueName: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - SHARP-CRESTED WEIR
description: A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - SHARP-CRESTED WEIR> is a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - WEIR> that is allowing the fluid to fall cleanly away from the weir. Sharp crested weirs are typically 1/4 inch or thinner metal plates

uniqueName: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - SINGLE JET
description: A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - SINGLE JET> is a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - VELOCITY> that consists of an impeller with radial vanes, impinged upon by a single jet

uniqueName: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - SONIC NOZZLE
description: A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - SONIC NOZZLE> is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT> that is operated by pressurizing the inlet of the venturi or evacuating the outlet in order to achieve an inlet-to-outlet pressure ratio of 1.4 to 1 or greater. This ratio maintains the nozzle in a choked or sonic state. In this state, only the upstream pressure and temperature influence the flow rate of gas through the nozzle. The flow rate through the nozzle becomes nearly a linear function of the inlet pressure which increases the thereby doubling the flow rate of gas
superclasses: INSTRUMENTATION ITEM, VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT

description: A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - SWIRL> is a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - VELOCITY> that uses swirls generated by fixed spiral vanes to measure flow
A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - TARGET> is a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - FORCE BALANCE> that uses a target, with force bar
superclasses: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - FORCE BALANCE

description: A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - ULTRASONIC> is a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - VELOCITY> based on ultrasonic technology
subclasses: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - ULTRASONIC DOPPLER, VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - ULTRASONIC IN-LINE, VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - ULTRASONIC TRANSIT TIME

uniqueName: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - ULTRASONIC DOPPLER
description: A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - ULTRASONIC DOPPLER> is a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - VELOCITY> that measures the Doppler shift resulting from reflecting an ultrasonic beam off the particulates in flowing fluid. The frequency of the transmitted beam is affected by the movement of the particles; this frequency shift can be used to calculate the fluid velocity. For the Doppler principle to work there must be a high enough density of sonically reflective materials such as solid particles or air bubbles suspended in the fluid

uniqueName: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - ULTRASONIC IN-LINE
description: A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - ULTRASONIC IN-LINE> is a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - VELOCITY> that is mounted in-line with a pipeline

uniqueName: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - ULTRASONIC TRANSIT TIME
description: A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - ULTRASONIC TRANSIT TIME> is a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - VELOCITY> that measures the difference of the transit time of ultrasonic pulses propagating in and against the direction of flow. uniqueName: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - VENTURI TUBE
description: A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - VENTURI TUBE> is a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE> that constricts the flow using a <VENTURI>, and pressure sensors measure the differential pressure before and within the constriction. This method is widely used to measure <VOLUME FLOW RATE> in the transmission of gas through pipelines
superclasses: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE

uniqueName: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - V-NOTCH WEIR
description: A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - V-NOTCH WEIR> is a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - WEIR> that is a triangular channel section, used to measure small discharge values. The upper edge of the section is always above the water level, so the channel is always triangular simplifying calculation of the cross-sectional area

A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - VORTEX> is a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - VELOCITY> that involves placing a bluff body (called a shedder bar) in the path of the fluid. As the fluid passes this bar, disturbances in the flow called vortices are created. The vortices trail behind the cylinder, alternatively from each side of the bluff body. The frequency at which these vortices alternate sides is essentially proportional to the flow rate of the fluid. Inside, atop, or downstream of the shedder bar is a sensor for measuring the frequency of the vortex shedding. This sensor is often a piezoelectric crystal, which produces a small, but measurable, voltage pulse every time a vortex is created. Since the frequency of such a voltage pulse is also proportional to the fluid velocity, a volumetric flow rate is calculated using the cross sectional area of the flow meter

A <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - WEIR> is a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - LEVEL-TO-FLOW OPEN CHANNEL> that is an obstruction in the flow path in an open channel. The weir will cause an increase in the water depth as the water flows over the weir. In general, the greater the flow rate, the greater will be the increase in depth of flow, The height of water above the top of the weir is the measurement usually used to correlate with flow rate
superclasses: VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - LEVEL-TO-FLOW OPEN CHANNEL

description: A <WEAR TEST DROP WEIGHT> is a <WEIGHT> as applied for a wear test
<WEARING> is the <Activity> of diminishing or impairing by use or attrition
A <WEATHER BARRIER> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <BARRIER> which is a layer of material (as roofing paper) used to retard or prevent air and water to be transported into insulation
A <WEATHER BEACON> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <BEACON> that indicates the local weather forecast in a code of colored or flashing lights. It is usually located on the roof of a tall building
A <WEATHER DATA COLLECTION EVENT> is an <Event> at which  the weather data  will be or has beencollected
A <WEATHER DECK> is  a <DECK> that is the uppermost continuous deck with no overhead protection
A <WEATHER LOUVER> is a <LOUVER> for the inlet or outlet of air used for ventilation
<WEATHER PROTECTING> is <PROTECTING> against the unwanted impact of weather
subclasses: TROPICALISING, WINTERISING

description: A <WEATHER REPORT ISSUE EVENT> is an <Event> at which  a weather report will be or has been issued
<WEAVING> is the <Activity> of forming by interlacing strands
A <WEB DATA STORAGE> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <DATA STORAGE> that is accessible via the internet
A <WEBER> is a <PropertyQuantification> between a <MAGNETIC FLUX> and a <NUMBER SPACE OF -INF TO +INF>

A <WEBER NUMBER> is a <RATIO> between the inertial force and the surface tension force, ndicating whether the kinetic or the surface tension energy is dominant. It is calculated as: We = rho.v^2.l/sigma where rho is <MASS DENSITY>, v is <SPEED>, l is <LENGTH> and sigma is surface tension
A <WEBSITE> is an <InformationObject> and a <REFERENCE(function)>, available on the internet, that provides information about a particular subject or range of subjects
A <WEDGE> is a <FACETED SOLID> and a <FACETED SOLID PRIMITIVE> in parallel planes
subclasses: CANONICALLY PARAMETERISED WEDGE, RIGHT ANGLED WEDGE

description: A <WEDGE GATE> is a <GATE VALVE CLOSURE MEMBER> that is wedge shaped.
subclasses: DOUBLE EXPANDING WEDGE GATE, FLEXIBLE WEDGE DISK, SINGLE EXPANDING WEDGE GATE, SOLID WEDGE DISC

uniqueName: WEDGE GATE BUTT WELDING END BODY

A <WEDGE GATE EXTENDED END BODY> is a <WEDGE GATE VALVE BODY> that has extended ends.
A <WEDGE GATE FLANGED END BODY> is a <WEDGE GATE VALVE BODY> that has flanged ends.
A <WEDGE GATE THREADED END BODY> is a <WEDGE GATE VALVE BODY> that has threaded ends.
A <WEDGE GATE VALVE> is a <GATE VALVE> that has a wedge closure member
subclasses: FLEXIBLE WEDGE GATE VALVE, RUBBER SEATED WEDGE GATE VALVE, SOFT SEATED WEDGE GATE VALVE, SOLID WEDGE GATE VALVE, SPLIT WEDGE GATE VALVE

description: A <WEDGE GATE VALVE BODY> is a <GATE VALVE BODY> which accomodates a wedge gate
subclasses: FLEXIBLE WEDGE GATE VALVE BODY, SOLID WEDGE GATE VALVE BODY, SPLIT WEDGE GATE VALVE BODY, WEDGE GATE BUTT WELDING END BODY, WEDGE GATE EXTENDED END BODY, WEDGE GATE FLANGED END BODY, WEDGE GATE THREADED END BODY

description: A <WEDGE SCREEN> is a <FILTER CARTRIDGE> and a <SCREEN> that contains a V-shape wire profile
A <WEDGE THREAD> is a <THREAD> that has a wedge shape.
A <WEEKS AFTER DELIVERY> is a <PropertyQuantification>
A <WEEKS AFTER ORDER> is a <PropertyQuantification>
A <WEEKS PRIOR TO DELIVERY> is a <PropertyQuantification>
<WEEPING> is the <Activity> of liquid coming out
A <WEIGH BRIDGE> is an <<ARTEFACT> and a <WEIGHER> for weighing loads carried by road or rail waggons
A <WEIGHER> is a <FunctionalObject> that is capable of <WEIGHING>
subclasses: BATCH WEIGHER, CONTINUOUS WEIGHER, WEIGH BRIDGE

description: <WEIGHING> is <MEASURING> a <MASS>
A <WEIGHING BALANCE> is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and a <WEIGHT MEASURING INSTRUMENT>, where <WEIGHT> is measured by <BALANCING> against a calibrated weight

A <WEIGHING PROCEDURE> is an <InformationObject> and a <PROCEDURE> and a <DOCUMENT> that details a method of recording weight during design and manufacture and a method of weighing equipment prior to shipment; A detailed definition of the <DATA> required in a particular context is given in the applicable instance of <DocumentDefinition>
A <WEIGHING SCALE> is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and a <WEIGHT MEASURING INSTRUMENT> where <WEIGHT> is directly measured rather than by balancing
A <WEIGHT> is a <FORCE> exerted on a body by gravity
subclasses: DRY WEIGHT, GROSS TOTAL WEIGHT, OPERATING WEIGHT, ROTOR ASSEMBLY WEIGHT, SHIPPING WEIGHT, TOTAL WEIGHT, UNIT WEIGHT, WEAR TEST DROP WEIGHT

uniqueName: WEIGHT  MEASURING INSTRUMENT - STRAIN GAUGE LOAD CELL
description: A <WEIGHT  MEASURING INSTRUMENT - STRAIN GAUGE LOAD CELL> is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and a <WEIGHT MEASURING INSTRUMENT> that handles the measurement results of a <STRAIN GAUGE LOAD CELL>
A <WEIGHT ACTUATOR> is an <ARTEFACT> and an <ACTUATOR> that is powered by the use of gravity forces
A <WEIGHT AND VOLUME ESTIMATES> is an <ESTIMATE> of weights and volumes for use in conceptual plant layout and civil/structural design
A <WEIGHT CALCULATION> is a <CALCULATION SHEET> with a record of a calculation of the <WEIGHT> of the material inside engineering material <SHAPE>s
A <WEIGHT CERTIFICATE> is a <CERTIFICATE> certifying the correct gross weight for a piece of equipment including packing materials.  This typically should also document the center of gravity
A <WEIGHT COATING> is a <COATING LAYER> that is used as a way to keep pipelines submerged whilst protecting them
A <WEIGHT DATA SHEET> is a <DATASHEET> that records the distribution of weight in a structure and shows the center of gravity of that structure
A <WEIGHT DATASHEET DEFINITION> is a <DATASHEET DEFINITION> for a <WEIGHT DATASHEET>
A <WEIGHT FRACTION OF GAS> is a <RATIO> of the <WEIGHT> fraction of gas in a gas/liquid phase to the <WEIGHT> of the total volume
A <WEIGHT ITEM> is an <ARTEFACT> that is supplied with a <WEIGHT DATA SHEET>
A <WEIGHT LOAD INDICATOR> is a <WEIGHT METER> that displays the weight of materials or products being lifted
A <WEIGHT MEASURING ELEMENT> is a <MEASURING ELEMENT> for the measurement of <WEIGHT> (mass)
subclasses: CAPACITIVE LOAD CELL, HYDRAULIC LOAD CELL, PNEUMATIC LOAD CELL, VIBRATING WIRE LOAD CELL

description: A <WEIGHT MEASURING INSTRUMENT> is a <MEASURING INSTRUMENT> for the measurement of <WEIGHT> (mass), that handles the measurement result from a <WEIGHT MEASURING ELEMENT>
subclasses: RATED CAPACITY INDICATOR, WEIGHING BALANCE, WEIGHING SCALE, WEIGHT  MEASURING INSTRUMENT - STRAIN GAUGE LOAD CELL, WEIGHT METER, WEIGHT SWITCH, WEIGHT TRANSMITTER

description: A <WEIGHT METER> is an <INSTRUMENTATION ITEM> and a <WEIGHT MEASURING INSTRUMENT> for weight measurements, usually with a hook to suspend the object to be weighed
subclasses: WEIGHT LOAD INDICATOR

description: A <WEIGHT METERING SYSTEM> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <FISCAL METERING SYSTEM> that measures the weight of a substance. Bulk material products (solids) are measured by weight in general
A <WEIGHT PER AREA> is an <UNIT WEIGHT> for a given area
A <WEIGHT PER LENGTH> is an <UNIT WEIGHT> for a given length
A <WEIGHT PER VOLUME> is an <UNIT WEIGHT> for a given volume
A <WEIGHT PERCENTAGE> is a <PERCENTAGE> where the calculation is based on a <RATIO> between weights
subclasses: WATER CUT - WEIGHT PERCENTAGE

description: A <WEIGHT REPORT> is a <REPORT> that shows weight and center of gravity of equipment. If large items are to be handled for equipment installation or maintenance, then the weight and center of gravity of these individual parts should be shown. Final weighing certificate shall accompany goods during shipment and delivery
A <WEIGHT SWITCH> is a <PROCESS SWITCH> and a <WEIGHT MEASURING INSTRUMENT>
subclasses: WEIGHT SWITCH WITH LOAD CELL

description: A <WEIGHT SWITCH WITH LOAD CELL> is a <WEIGHT SWITCH> that uses a <LOAD CELL>
A <WEIGHT TRANSMITTER>is a <PROCESS VARIABLE TRANSMITTER> and a <WEIGHT MEASURING INSTRUMENT>
superclasses: PROCESS VARIABLE TRANSMITTER, WEIGHT MEASURING INSTRUMENT

description: A <WEIGHTED ACCUMULATOR>> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <HYDRAULIC ACCUMULATOR> where the chock absorbing capabilities are achieved by applying a weight

A <WEIGHTED AVERAGE BOILING TEMPERATURE> is an <IndirectProperty> that refers to a <BOILING TEMPERATURE> that is the average of the boiling temperatures of a number of fractions, averaged proportional to the weights of those fractions

A <WEIGHT-LOADED VALVE> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <VALVE> in which the closure member is held against the seat by a static weight. The valve opens when the internal fluid pressure the valve is exposed to is higher than the force the weight creates in the valve
A <WEIGHT-OPERATED RELIEF VALVE> is a <RELIEF VALVE> in which the closure member is held against the seat by a static weight
A <WEIR> is a <PLATE> intended to establish a liquid level
subclasses: INLET WEIR, OUTLET WEIR

description: A <WEIR DISTRIBUTOR> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <DISTRIBUTOR> that has weirs as parts to guide the fluid
subclasses: WEIR TROUGH DISTRIBUTOR

description: A <WEIR FLOW METER> is a <VOLUME FLOW MEASURING ELEMENT - AREA-VELOCITY> utilizing some kind of weir as obstruction
A <WEIR TROUGH DISTRIBUTOR> is a <WEIR DISTRIBUTOR> that includes troughs made from weirs to guide the fluid
A <WELD> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <CONNECTOR> that is made by applying weld material in a <WELDING> activity
A <WELD FEATURE> is a <Feature> that is in the body or the heat affected zone of a weld
A <WELD LEG LENGTH> is a <STRAIGHT LINEAR DISTANCE> which is the leg <LENGTH> of a <WELD>

A <WELD MAP> is an <InformationObject> and a <MAP> that is an outline drawing that usually identifies all welds and relates them to the relevant welding procedure number and non destructive testing requirements
A <WELD NECK COMPACT FLANGE> is a <COMPACT PIPE FLANGE> and a <WELD NECK FLANGE>
superclasses: COMPACT PIPE FLANGE, WELD NECK FLANGE

description: A <WELD NECK FLANGE> is a <PIPE FLANGE> where the non-flanged end is a hub or neck with a butt welding end.
subclasses: WELD NECK COMPACT FLANGE, WELD NECK FLAT FACE FLANGE, WELD NECK GROOVE FACE FLANGE, WELD NECK MALE FACE FLANGE, WELD NECK ORIFICE FLANGE, WELD NECK RAISED FACE FLANGE, WELD NECK RECESS FLANGE, WELD NECK RING JOINT FLANGE, WELD NECK SPIGOT FLANGE, WELD NECK TONGUE FACE FLANGE

description: A <WELD NECK FLANGE HUB> is a <PIPE FLANGE HUB> that is part of a weld neck flange.
A <WELD NECK FLAT FACE FLANGE> is a <FLAT FACE FLANGE> and a <WELD NECK FLANGE>
superclasses: FLAT FACE FLANGE, WELD NECK FLANGE

description: A <WELD NECK GROOVE FACE FLANGE> is a <GROOVE FLANGE> and a <WELD NECK FLANGE> where the flanged end is a groove face flanged end.
A <WELD NECK MALE FACE FLANGE> is a <WELD NECK FLANGE> where the flanged end is a male face flanged end.
A <WELD NECK ORIFICE FLANGE> is a <ORIFICE FLANGE> and a <WELD NECK FLANGE>
A <WELD NECK ORIFICE FLANGE SET> is a <PIPING COMPONENT> that is an assembly of a <WELD NECK ORIFICE FLANGE>s
A <WELD NECK RAISED FACE FLANGE> is a <RAISED FACE FLANGE> and a <WELD NECK FLANGE>
superclasses: RAISED FACE FLANGE, WELD NECK FLANGE

description: A <WELD NECK RECESS FLANGE> is a <RECESS FLANGE> and a <WELD NECK FLANGE>
A <WELD NECK RING JOINT FLANGE> is a <RING JOINT FLANGE> and a <WELD NECK FLANGE>
superclasses: RING JOINT FLANGE, WELD NECK FLANGE

description: A <WELD NECK SPIGOT FLANGE> is a <SPIGOT FLANGE> and a <WELD NECK FLANGE> that is a weld neck flange where the flanged end is a spigot face flanged end
A <WELD NECK TONGUE FACE FLANGE> is a <TONGUE FLANGE> and a <WELD NECK FLANGE>
A <WELD NUT> is a <NUT> that is manufactured from low carbon steel intended to be welded onto a plate or machine element to give hold for a bolt or screw
subclasses: HEXAGONAL WELD NUT, SQUARE WELD NUT

description: A <WELD OVERLAY> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <LINING> made by welding
A <WELD TEST PLATE> is a <PLATE> used for welding procedure qualification and testing of welds
subclasses: PRODUCTION WELD TEST PLATE

description: A <WELD THROAT THICKNESS> is a <THICKNESS> that is of the throat of a <WELD>
A <WELDABLE STEEL> is a <STEEL> which can be welded without special precautions
<WELDED> is an <INDIVIDUAL WITH A STATUS> in a state of being or having been subjected to <WELDING>

description: A <WELDED ARTEFACT> is a <WROUGHT ARTEFACT> with a <WELDED> (Status) which has been manufactured by welding
A <WELDED CASING> is a <CASING> that is constructed and fabricated by welding of parts.
A <WELDED CYLINDER COLUMN> is a <CYLINDER COLUMN> (cylinder block) that is entirely made of welded steel.

A <WELDED FLANGE THERMOWELL> is a <FLANGED THERMOWELL> where the flange is welded to the thermowell shank/stem.
A <WELDED IMPELLER> is an <ARTEFACT> and an <IMPELLER> that is constructed and fabricated by welding of parts
A <WELDED JOINT> is an <ARTEFACT> with a <JOINT> that is joined by <WELDING>

description: A <WELDED NOZZLE> is a <NOZZLE> that consists of components welded together, in contrast with a forged nozzle
A <WELDED PADDLE ORIFICE PLATE> is a <PADDLE ORIFICE PLATE> where the orifce plate and the paddle (handle) is assembled through welding
A <WELDED PIPE> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <PIPE> and been manufactured from shaped plate, sheet or strips by a welding process
subclasses: CONTINUOUS-WELDED PIPE, ELECTRIC WELDED PIPE, GMAW WELDED PIPE, HELICAL SEAM WELDED PIPE, STRAIGHT SEAM WELDED PIPE

A <WELDED THERMOWELL> is a <THERMOWELL> that is designed for being welded on to a vessel or pipe.
A <WELDED THERMOWELL FLANGE> is a <THERMOWELL INTEGRAL FLANGE> where the flange is made by &amp;#39;welding&amp;#39;

A <WELDED TOOL JOINT DRILL PIPE> is a <DRILL PIPE> made up of two <TOOL JOINT WELDED MEMBER>s, one of which is a one of which is a <TOOL JOINT PIN MEMBER>, the other a <TOOL JOINT BOX MEMBER>, the three together making up a welded tool drill pipe.
A <WELDED VALVE BONNET> is a <VALVE BONNET> that is welded to the valve body.
A <WELDER> is a <FunctionalObject> that is capable of <WELDING>
subclasses: AWS CERTIFIED WELDER

<WELDING> is the <Activity> of joining materials by a process that produces coalescence of materials by heating them to suitable temperatures with or without the application of pressure or by the application of pressure alone and with or without the use of filler material
subclasses: ARC WELDING, ELECTRICAL WELDING, ELECTROSLAG WELDING, FUSION WELDING, REPAIR WELDING, RESISTANCE WELDING, SOLID STATE WELDING, SUBMERGED WELDING, WELDING TO AWS D1.1

A <WELDING BOSS> is an <OLET> that is a short piece of pipe with one end shaped for welding to the main run pipe.

A <WELDING END DRILL PIPE BODY> is a <DRILL PIPE BODY> designed to be connected to <TOOL JOINT THREADED MEMBER>s, one of which is a <TOOL JOINT PIN MEMBER>, the other a <TOOL JOINT BOX MEMBER>, the three together making up a drill pipe.
A <WELDING END TRANSITION> is a <Feature> that is where <WELDING END TRANSITION>s from the full wall thickness to a bevelled end of lesser thickness than the full wall thickness
A <WELDING END VALVE BODY> is a <VALVE BODY> that has inlet and/or outlet welding ends
subclasses: ANGLE VALVE BODY BUTT WELDING END, STRAIGHT VALVE BODY BUTT WELDING END, VALVE BODY BUTT WELDING END

description: A <WELDING PROCEDURE QUALIFICATION> is an <InformationObject> and a <DOCUMENT> that describes the parameters used in qualification of Welding Procedures together with mechanical testing results

A <WELDING PROCEDURE SPECIFICATION> is a <SPECIFICATION> that is the formal written document describing welding procedures, which provides direction to the welder or welding operators for making sound and quality production welds as per the code requirements
A <WELDING PROCEDURE SPECIFICATION DEFINITION> is a <SPECIFICATION DEFINITION> that defines the rules for the contents of a specification about a welding procedure and process
A <WELDING REPAIR PROCEDURE> is an <InformationObject> and a <PROCEDURE> and a <DOCUMENT> describING a set of logically sequenced instructions to execute a weld repair
A <WELDING ROD> is a <CONSTRUCTION  MATERIAL> that is filler metal in the form of a wire or rod
A <WELDING ROD DRYING OVEN> is an <ARTEFACT> and an <OVEN> and a <DRYER> that is intended for drying welding rods (electrodes)
A <WELDING SOCKET> is an <ELECTRICAL SOCKET> intended for <WELDING SET>.
<WELDING TO AWS D1.1> is <WELDING> in accordance with <AWS D1.1>
A <WELDING TRANSFORMER> is a <POWER TRANSFORMER> that is intended to provide power for electric arc welding.
A <WELDING UNIT> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <TOOL> for arc welding, either AC or DC, comprising a supply unit and a regulator
subclasses: PORTABLE SMAW WELDING UNIT, PORTABLE TIG WELDING UNIT, STATIONARY TIG WELDING UNIT

description: A <WELDOFLANGE> is an <OLET> that makes a 90-degree branch and that has a flanged end at the branch end.
A <WELDOLET> is an <OLET> and a <PIPING NETWORK NODE> that is making a 90-degree branch and has a butt welding end on branch
A <WELL> is a <FunctionalObject> that is arranged to obtain or produce from, or store or inject a material into, the earth
subclasses: ABANDONED WELL, ACTIVE WELL, ARTESIAN WELL, BLOWOUT RELIEF WELL, BOREHOLE REACQUISITION WELL, CLOSED WELL, DRILLING SUSPENDED WELL, DRILLING WELL, DRY WELL, EXPLORATION WELL, FLUID STORAGE WELL, GENERAL SERVICE WELL, HIGH PRESSURE HIGH TEMPERATURE WELL, INJECTION WELL, MINERAL WELL, OBSERVATION WELL, OPEN WELL, PERMITTED WELL, PLUGGED WELL, PRODUCTION WELL, PROPOSED WELL, RE-ENTRY WELL, REMEDIAL SIDETRACK WELL, SUSPENDED WELL, TEST WELL, TIGHT WELL, WASTE DISPOSAL WELL, WATER DISPOSAL WELL

description: A <WELL ABANDONMENT EVENT> is an <ENDING EVENT> at which operations of a well will be or has been ceased permanently
A <WELL ASSEMBLY> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <SYSTEM> that is an assembly of equipment for the exploitation of underground resources
subclasses: ARTIFICIAL LIFT WELL ASSEMBLY, HORIZONTAL CHRISTMAS TREE WELL ASSEMBLY, INTELLIGENT WELL ASSEMBLY, MULTILATERAL WELL ASSEMBLY, MULTIZONE WELL ASSEMBLY, SATELLITE WELL ASSEMBLY, SUBSEA WELL ASSEMBLY, SURFACE WELL ASSEMBLY, TEMPLATE WELL ASSEMBLY, VERTICAL CHRISTMAS TREE WELL ASSEMBLY

subclasses: WELL CASING ASSEMBLY, WELL CONDUCTOR CASING, WELL INTERMEDIATE CASING, WELL PRODUCTION CASING, WELL SURFACE CASING

description: A <WELL CASING ASSEMBLY> is a <WELL COMPLETION ASSEMBLY> and a <WELL CASING> that is an assembly of casing pies, casing hanger and seals that is lowered into a well, and provides structural support for the borehole.
subclasses: RECIPROCATED WELL CASING ASSEMBLY, ROTATED WELL CASING ASSEMBLY, WELL CONDUCTOR CASING ASSEMBLY, WELL INTERMEDIATE CASING ASSEMBLY, WELL PRODUCTION CASING ASSEMBLY, WELL SURFACE CASING ASSEMBLY

description: <WELL CASING ASSEMBLY RECIPROCATION> is the <Activity> of well completion assembly reciprocation that is applied to the well casing string during the wellbore cementing job to help in removal of drilling fluid and efficient placement of the cement slurry

<WELL CASING ASSEMBLY ROTATION> is the <Activity> of well completion assembly rotationtion that is applied to the well casing string during the wellbore cementing job to help in removal of drilling fluid and efficient placement of the cement slurry
A <WELL CASING CUTTER> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <CUTTER> using rotating knives to cut a hole in well casing
A <WELL CASING HEAD> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <COVER> that is a heavy, flanged steel fitting which is fixed to the top of the casing set in a well
subclasses: WELL CASING HEAD FLANGED END, WELL CASING HEAD HUB END, WELL CASING HEAD STUDDED OUTLET, WELL CASING HEAD THREADED END, WELL CASING HEAD THREADED OUTLET, WELL CASING HEAD WELDED END

uniqueName: WELL CASING HEAD EXTERNALLY THREADED END
description: A <WELL CASING HEAD EXTERNALLY THREADED END> is a <WELL CASING HEAD THREADED END> that has an externally threaded end for connection to a casing pipe with an internally threaded end.
A <WELL CASING HEAD FLANGED END> is a <WELL CASING HEAD> that has a flanged upper end.
A <WELL CASING HEAD HUB END> is a <WELL CASING HEAD> that has a hub-type upper end.

uniqueName: WELL CASING HEAD INTERNALLY THREADED END
description: A <WELL CASING HEAD INTERNALLY THREADED END> is a <WELL CASING HEAD THREADED END> that has an internally threaded end for connection to a casing pipe with an externally threaded end.
A <WELL CASING HEAD STUDDED OUTLET> is a <WELL CASING HEAD> that has side outlets that have studded bolts for flanged connection.
A <WELL CASING HEAD THREADED END> is a <WELL CASING HEAD> that has a threaded end for connection to a casing pipe threaded end.
subclasses: WELL CASING HEAD EXTERNALLY THREADED END, WELL CASING HEAD INTERNALLY THREADED END

description: A <WELL CASING HEAD THREADED OUTLET> is a <WELL CASING HEAD> that has side outlets which have internal threads.
A <WELL CASING HEAD WELDED END> is a <WELL CASING HEAD> that has a welded end for connection to a casing pipe by welding.
A <WELL CASING STRING> is a <DRILLING COMPONENT> that consists of pipes assembled end to end that is intended to line the walls of a drilled well.
subclasses: WELL CONDUCTOR CASING STRING

description: A <WELL CASING STRING SIZE DESIGNATION> is a <NOMINAL SIZE DESIGNATION> that is a nominal outside diameter value of a well casing string
<WELL CEMENT PLUGGING> is the <Activity> of activities related to pumping cement and setting abandonment plugs, including time to reverse out cement and to test the plugs
A <WELL CLUSTER> is an <ARTEFACT> and a <SYSTEM> that consists of a number of individual wells making up or considered a unit
A <WELL COMMISSIONING STARTING EVENT> is an <Event> at which the commissioning of the well started
<WELL COMPLETION> is the <Activity> of outfitting of a <WELLBORE>
A <WELL COMPLETION ASSEMBLY> is a <DRILLING COMPONENT> that is an assembly of downhole tubulars and equipment required to enable safe and efficient production from an oil or gas well.
subclasses: WELL CASING ASSEMBLY, WELL TUBING ASSEMBLY

description: <WELL COMPLETION ASSEMBLY RECIPROCATION> is the <Activity> of alternately raising and lowering the well completion assembly, i.e. drillstring, casing string or liner in the wellbore

<WELL COMPLETION ASSEMBLY ROTATION> is the <Activity> of rotating the a well completion assembly, i.e. drillstring, casing string or liner in the wellbore.that is applied to the well casing string during the wellbore cementing job to help in removal of drilling fluid and efficient placement of the cement slurry

uniqueName: WELL COMPLETION BOP AND WELLHEAD OPERATIONS
description: <WELL COMPLETION BOP AND WELLHEAD OPERATIONS> is the <Activity> of activities related to running/installing/testing/removing/retrieving <BOP>s, risers, spools, wellhead plugs and valves, <X->mas trees etc

uniqueName: WELL COMPLETION CIRCULATING AND CONDITIONING ACTIVITY
description: <WELL COMPLETION CIRCULATING AND CONDITIONING ACTIVITY> is the <Activity> of activities related to circulation/conditioning/displacement of drilling/completion/workover fluid and planned killing of well
<WELL COMPLETION COIL TUBING RIGING> is the <Activity> of activities related to prepartion and riging snubbing and coil tubing equipment up and down related to completion, including pressure testing
<WELL COMPLETION FLOW TESTING> is the <Activity> of activities related to initial flow/clean up/flow test/build up of well after perforating/stimulating/temporary artificial lift during completion
<WELL COMPLETION MILLING> is <MILLING> or grinding to remove junk in the hole or to grind away all or part of a casing string during completion operations
<WELL COMPLETION OTHER ACTIVITY> is the <Activity> of uncategorised activities related to well completion
<WELL COMPLETION PERFORATING ACTIVITY> is the <Activity> of activities related running/firing/pulling of perforating guns/detonating bar and related rigging up/down and testing of wire line equipment
<WELL COMPLETION SAND CONTROL> is the <Activity> of activities related to sand control during well completion
<WELL COMPLETION SCSSV TESTING> is <TESTING <SCSSV> during completion independently from the <SCSSV> running procedure
